rules.name: Virtual Link Communication Requirement

constraint.value: End systems must communicate through virtual links

rules.source_quote: Virtual Link
rules.test_hint: Generate frames that attempt to communicate without using virtual links or violate virtual link constraints

rules.name: Flow and Traffic Control Requirement

constraint.value: Network must implement flow and traffic control mechanisms

rules.source_quote: Flow/Traffic Control
rules.test_hint: Generate traffic that exceeds flow control limits or violates traffic control policies

rules.name: Frame Scheduling Requirement

constraint.value: End systems must implement frame scheduling mechanisms

rules.source_quote: Scheduling
rules.test_hint: Generate frames that violate scheduling constraints or attempt to bypass scheduling mechanisms

rules.name: MAC Destination Address Requirement

constraint.value: Frames must have valid MAC destination addresses

rules.source_quote: MAC Destination Address
rules.test_hint: Generate frames with invalid, malformed, or inappropriate MAC destination addresses

rules.name: MAC Source Address Requirement

constraint.value: Frames must have valid MAC source addresses

rules.source_quote: MAC Source Address
rules.test_hint: Generate frames with invalid, malformed, or spoofed MAC source addresses

rules.name: Sequence Number Generation Requirement

constraint.value: Sending end systems must generate sequence numbers

rules.source_quote: Sequence Numbers and the Sending End System
rules.test_hint: Generate frames with missing, duplicate, or out-of-sequence sequence numbers

rules.name: Integrity Checking Requirement

constraint.value: Receiving end systems must perform integrity checking

rules.source_quote: Integrity Checking
rules.test_hint: Generate frames with corrupted data or invalid integrity markers to test integrity checking mechanisms

rules.name: Redundancy Management Requirement

constraint.value: Receiving end systems must implement redundancy management

rules.source_quote: Redundancy Management
rules.test_hint: Generate conflicting frames on redundant paths or violate redundancy management protocols

rules.name: Frame filtering function requirement

constraint.value: switches must implement frame filtering function

rules.source_quote: Frame Filtering
rules.test_hint: Send frames that should be filtered and verify they are dropped by the switch

rules.name: Traffic policing function requirement

constraint.value: switches must implement traffic policing function

rules.source_quote: Traffic Policing
rules.test_hint: Send traffic that exceeds policing parameters and verify it is dropped or rate-limited by the switch

rules.name: Policing and filtering parameters requirement

constraint.value: switches must implement policing and filtering parameters

rules.source_quote: Policing and Filtering Parameters
rules.test_hint: Configure invalid or missing policing/filtering parameters and verify switch behavior

rules.name: Frame Filtering Function Required

constraint.value: AFDX switches must implement frame filtering functionality

rules.source_quote: 4.2.1  Frame Filtering
rules.test_hint: Send frames to a switch and verify that filtering rules are applied correctly - test with frames that should be filtered vs. forwarded

rules.name: Traffic Policing Function Required

constraint.value: AFDX switches must implement traffic policing functionality

rules.source_quote: 4.2.2  Traffic Policing
rules.test_hint: Send traffic at rates exceeding configured limits to verify policing enforcement - test with bursts and sustained rates above BAG limits

rules.name: Switching Function Required

constraint.value: AFDX switches must implement switching functionality

rules.source_quote: 4.4 Switching Function
rules.test_hint: Send frames to verify proper switching behavior - frames should be forwarded to correct output ports based on destination MAC addresses

rules.name: Switch End System Function Required

constraint.value: AFDX switches must implement end system functionality

rules.source_quote: 4.5 Switch End System Function
rules.test_hint: Test switch's ability to act as an end system - verify it can generate and receive management or control traffic

rules.name: Monitoring Function Required

constraint.value: AFDX switches must implement monitoring functionality

rules.source_quote: 4.6 Monitoring Function
rules.test_hint: Verify that switches provide monitoring capabilities for network health and performance tracking

rules.name: INIT Operating Mode Required

constraint.value: AFDX devices must support INIT operating mode

rules.source_quote: 4.8.2  INIT
rules.test_hint: Test device behavior during initialization - verify proper startup sequence and that device enters operational state correctly

rules.name: OPS Operating Mode Required

constraint.value: AFDX devices must support OPS (Operational) mode

rules.source_quote: 4.8.3  OPS: Operational Mode
rules.test_hint: Test normal operational behavior - verify device processes frames correctly when in operational mode

rules.name: Data Loading Mode Required

constraint.value: AFDX devices must support DL (Data Loading) mode

rules.source_quote: 4.8.4  DL: Data loading Mode
rules.test_hint: Test configuration loading behavior - verify device accepts configuration updates in data loading mode and rejects them in other modes

rules.name: AFDX protocol layer requirements
rules.source_quote: The requirements listed in this document aim at specifying interoperable functional elements: • Data link: MAC, VL addressing concept • Network: IP, ICMP • Transport: UDP, TCP (optional) • Network application layers: Sampling, Queuing, SAP, TFTP and SNMP
rules.test_hint: Send frames that violate the required protocol stack layers or use protocols not in the specified list

rules.name: TCP transport protocol optionality
rules.source_quote: Transport: UDP, TCP (optional)
rules.test_hint: Send TCP frames to devices that may not implement TCP support and verify proper handling

rules.name: AFDX LRU network interoperability requirement

constraint.value: any AFDX compliant LRU can connect to any AFDX network

rules.source_quote: This means that any AFDX compliant LRU (including switch) can be connected to any AFDX network, as far as the Form and Fit requirements (specific to the System and not specified in this document) are respected.
rules.test_hint: Test cross-vendor LRU compatibility by connecting devices from different manufacturers and verifying proper network operation

rules.name: Physical layer specification requirement
rules.source_quote: Physical layer is not specified here, but should be any of the ARINC 664 Part 2 defined solutions.
rules.test_hint: Test network behavior with physical layer implementations that do not conform to ARINC 664 Part 2

rules.name: AFDX deterministic network communication capability

constraint.value: deterministic network may communicate with wider profiled network and compliant network through routers or gateways

rules.source_quote: A deterministic network may communicate with a wider profiled network and by inference, with a compliant network through routers or gateways.
rules.test_hint: Test inter-network communication by sending frames between AFDX deterministic network and profiled/compliant networks through gateways to verify proper routing and protocol translation

rules.name: timely delivery requirement

constraint.value: quality of service including timely delivery is paramount

rules.source_quote: Part 7 describes a subset of this network, where quality of service including timely delivery is paramount.
rules.test_hint: Test by introducing delays in frame transmission or processing to verify network maintains timely delivery requirements and handles timing violations appropriately

rules.name: complete and up-to-date data delivery requirement

constraint.value: complete and up to date data delivered from source to receiver in a timely fashion

rules.source_quote: Control systems generally, and avionics systems in particular, rely on having complete and up to date data delivered from source to receiver in a timely fashion.
rules.test_hint: Test by fragmenting data, sending stale data, or introducing data corruption to verify network ensures data completeness and currency requirements

rules.name: real-time communication reliability requirement

constraint.value: reliable real time communication links are essential for safety critical systems

rules.source_quote: For safety critical systems reliable "real time" communication links are essential.
rules.test_hint: Test by introducing communication failures, timing jitter, or reliability issues to verify network maintains real-time communication guarantees for safety-critical applications

rules.name: total_latency_formula

constraint.value: L = Ts + Tm + Tr

rules.source_quote: and the total latency, L, is :  L = Ts + Tm + Tr
rules.test_hint: A fuzzer could generate frames with timing that violates expected latency bounds or measure actual vs calculated latency

rules.name: jitter_time_formula

constraint.value: Tj = (8 x M) / Nbw + Tmin_gap

rules.source_quote: Tj = (8 x M) / Nbw + Tmin_gap(it is assumed that the frames are of equal size).
rules.test_hint: A fuzzer could send frames of different sizes simultaneously to a switch to test if jitter calculations are correctly applied

rules.name: first_frame_latency_formula

constraint.value: La = Ts + Tm1 + Tsw + (8 x M)/Nbw + Tm2 + Tr

rules.source_quote: Latency for the first frame:  La = Ts + Tm1 + Tsw + ( 8 x M )/Nbw + Tm2 + Tr
rules.test_hint: A fuzzer could measure actual first frame latency and compare against calculated values to verify proper switch behavior

rules.name: delayed_frame_latency_formula

constraint.value: Lb = La + Tj

rules.source_quote: Latency for the delayed frame:  Lb = La + Tj
rules.test_hint: A fuzzer could send simultaneous frames to test if the second frame experiences the correct additional jitter delay

rules.name: simultaneous_frame_sequencing

constraint.value: simultaneous reception of frames must be dealt with by sequencing the frames for re-transmission

rules.source_quote: Simultaneous reception of frames from ESa and ESb at the switch will be dealt with by sequencing the two frames for re-transmission to ES c
rules.test_hint: A fuzzer could send simultaneous frames to a switch and verify they are properly sequenced rather than dropped or corrupted

rules.name: complete_frame_buffering

constraint.value: switches must buffer complete frames due to store and forward capacity

rules.source_quote: The contention in the switch and the store and forward capacity results in the need to buffer complete frames.
rules.test_hint: A fuzzer could send partial frames or oversized frames to test if the switch properly buffers complete frames before forwarding

rules.name: switch_latency_traffic_dependency

constraint.value: total switch latency (Tw) depends on traffic flow for the specific output port

rules.source_quote: Tw, referenced to an output port, depends on the traffic flow for that output port
rules.test_hint: A fuzzer could vary traffic loads on different output ports and verify that latency varies accordingly per port

rules.name: Virtual Link Maximum Bandwidth Constraint

constraint.value: Lmax/TGAP

rules.source_quote: The maximum bandwidth allocated to this VL is: Lmax/TGAP.
rules.test_hint: Send frames on a VL that exceed the Lmax/TGAP bandwidth limit over any time interval

rules.name: Exact Bandwidth Regulated Traffic Control

constraint.value: bounded_arrival_distribution

rules.source_quote: frame delivery follows a bounded arrival distribution. This bounded arrival implies exact bandwidth regulated traffic control.
rules.test_hint: Generate frame arrivals that violate bounded arrival distribution patterns, such as burst traffic exceeding bandwidth limits

rules.name: Virtual Link Bandwidth and Frame Interval Bounds

constraint.value: bounded_bandwidth_and_frame_interval

rules.source_quote: This is achieved by bounding both the bandwidth and the frame delivery interval for each VL.
rules.test_hint: Violate VL bandwidth bounds or send frames outside the defined frame delivery interval

rules.name: Frame Order Preservation Within Virtual Link

constraint.value: maintain_ordinal_integrity_within_VL

rules.source_quote: For this reason AFDX requires ordinal integrity of frames within a Virtual Link.
rules.test_hint: Send frames on a VL and verify they arrive in the same order, or deliberately reorder frames to test violation detection

rules.name: Single Service Class Requirement
rules.source_quote: Therefore, the only service class needed in the Aircraft Network is a guaranteed service.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to configure or use service classes other than guaranteed service

rules.name: End-to-End Delay Upper Bound Guarantee

constraint.value: mathematically_provable_upper_bound

rules.source_quote: A guaranteed service provides a firm, mathematically provable, upper bound on end-to-end frame transit delay.
rules.test_hint: Generate network conditions that could cause frame transit delays to exceed the calculated upper bound

rules.name: Constant Bandwidth Guarantee

constraint.value: constant_bandwidth_guarantee

rules.source_quote: Hence a guaranteed service provides both upper bounded delay and constant bandwidth leading to a logical open connection between one transmitting node and one or more receiving nodes.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to vary or reduce the allocated bandwidth below the guaranteed constant level

rules.name: Single source per VL constraint

constraint.value: only_one_source_per_vl

rules.source_quote: Only one End System within the Avionics network should be the source of any one VL.
rules.test_hint: Generate frames with the same VL ID but from multiple different source end systems

rules.name: Bandwidth isolation between VLs

constraint.value: bandwidth_isolation_required

rules.source_quote: The ES should provide logical isolation with respect to available bandwidth among the Virtual Link(s) it supports. Regardless of the attempted utilisation of a VL by one partition, the available Bandwidth on any other VL is unaffected.
rules.test_hint: Send high-rate traffic on one VL and verify it doesn't affect bandwidth of other VLs

rules.name: Frame ordering preservation

constraint.value: maintain_ordinal_integrity

rules.source_quote: For each Virtual Link, the End System should maintain the ordering of data as delivered by a partition, for both transmission and reception (ordinal integrity).
rules.test_hint: Send frames with sequence numbers out of order and verify the ES maintains proper ordering

rules.name: BAG frame rate limiting

constraint.value: max_one_frame_per_bag_interval

rules.source_quote: On a per VL basis the traffic regulator (traffic shaping function) should shape the flow to send no more than one frame in each interval of BAG milliseconds
rules.test_hint: Send multiple frames within a single BAG interval on the same VL

rules.name: Maximum frame size support
rules.source_quote: The End System should accommodate VL frames up to a size of 1518 bytes in both transmission and reception.
rules.test_hint: Send frames larger than 1518 bytes and verify they are rejected or handled appropriately

rules.name: BAG value range constraint
rules.source_quote: The Traffic shaping function of the ES should be able to handle BAG values in range 1 ms to 128 ms.
rules.test_hint: Configure VL with BAG values outside the 1-128 ms range

rules.name: Maximum bandwidth calculation

constraint.value: Lmax / BAG

rules.source_quote: The maximum usable bandwidth = Lmax / BAG in Kbytes per seconds.
rules.test_hint: Send traffic exceeding the calculated maximum bandwidth (Lmax/BAG) for a VL

rules.name: End System transmission technological latency bound
rules.source_quote: The technological latency of the end-system in transmission should be bounded and lower than 150 μs + frame delay.
rules.test_hint: Generate frames and measure transmission latency to ensure it exceeds 150 μs plus frame delay, violating the bound

rules.name: End System reception technological latency bound
rules.source_quote: The technological latency of the end-system in reception should be bounded and lower than 150 μs.
rules.test_hint: Generate frames and measure reception latency to ensure it exceeds 150 μs, violating the bound

rules.name: Maximum frame rate processing requirement
rules.source_quote: Equivalent to a duration of 6.72 μs per frame (about 148800 frames per second).
rules.test_hint: Generate frames at rates exceeding 148800 frames per second to test if the system can handle the load

rules.name: Minimum frame overhead calculation
rules.source_quote: 64 bytes (frame) + 12 bytes (IFG) + 7 bytes (Preamble) + 1 byte (SFD) = 84 bytes to transmit at 100 Mbits/s.
rules.test_hint: Generate frames with incorrect overhead calculations or violate the IFG, preamble, or SFD requirements

rules.name: Minimum frame transmission duration
rules.source_quote: Equivalent to a duration of 6.72 μs per frame (about 148800 frames per second).
rules.test_hint: Generate frames with transmission durations shorter than 6.72 μs to violate timing constraints

rules.name: Back-to-back frame transmission requirement
rules.source_quote: Transmit frames back to back
rules.test_hint: Generate continuous frame streams without proper inter-frame gaps to test back-to-back transmission limits

rules.name: Full frame rate reception processing requirement
rules.source_quote: Process received frames at full frame rate of the medium and appropriate (selected) frames are made available to the partition at full frame rate of the medium
rules.test_hint: Send frames at maximum rate to test if the system can process all frames without dropping any

rules.name: Maximum jitter bound limit
rules.source_quote: In all cases, the jitter is bounded at 500μs to limit the impact on determinism for the whole network.
rules.test_hint: Generate transmission patterns that would cause jitter to exceed 500 μs to test jitter bounds enforcement

rules.name: Minimum technological jitter baseline
rules.source_quote: 40 μs is a typical minimum fixed technological jitter
rules.test_hint: Measure jitter values below 40 μs to test if the system enforces the minimum technological jitter baseline

rules.name: Single frame maximum latency constraint

constraint.value: MAX_Latency_i ≤ BAG_i + Max_jitter + Technological_Latency_in_transmission

rules.source_quote: the total allowed latency for a given VLi is: MAX_Latency i ≤ BAG i + Max_jitter + Technological_Latency_in_transmission
rules.test_hint: Generate frames that arrive with latency exceeding BAG + Max_jitter + Technological_Latency_in_transmission

rules.name: MAC destination address must be group address

constraint.value: least significant bit of first byte must be 1

rules.source_quote: The least significant bit of the first byte indicates the group address (always = 1)
rules.test_hint: Send frames with MAC destination address where the LSB of first byte is 0 (individual address)

rules.name: MAC destination address must be locally administered

constraint.value: second to least significant bit of first byte must be 1

rules.source_quote: The second to least significant bit of the first byte indicates the locally administered address (always = 1)
rules.test_hint: Send frames with MAC destination address where the second LSB of first byte is 0 (globally administered)

rules.name: MAC source address must be individual address

constraint.value: least significant bit of first byte must be 0

rules.source_quote: The least significant bit of the first byte indicates the Individual Address = 0
rules.test_hint: Send frames with MAC source address where the LSB of first byte is 1 (group address)

rules.name: MAC source address must be locally administered

constraint.value: second to least significant bit of first byte must be 1

rules.source_quote: The second to least significant bit of the first byte indicates the locally administered address = 1
rules.test_hint: Send frames with MAC source address where the second LSB of first byte is 0 (globally administered)

rules.name: MAC source constant field value
rules.source_quote: The Constant field is set to "0000 0010 0000 0000 0000 0000" as shown in Figure 3-11
rules.test_hint: Send frames with MAC source addresses that have different constant field values

rules.name: Interface_ID allowed values
rules.source_quote: 0 0 1 The Ethernet MAC controller is connected to the network A, 0 1 0 The Ethernet MAC controller is connected to the network B
rules.test_hint: Send frames with Interface_ID values other than 001 or 010 (e.g., 000, 011, 100, 101, 110, 111)

rules.name: Default mode dual network transmission

constraint.value: each frame is sent across both of two networks

rules.source_quote: In default mode each frame is sent across both of two networks.
rules.test_hint: Send frame on only one network or more than two networks to violate this rule

rules.name: First valid wins reception policy

constraint.value: first frame to be received from either network with the next valid sequence number is accepted and passed up the stack

rules.source_quote: Upon reception, an algorithm in the communications stack (below IP layer) uses a "First Valid wins" policy. This means that the first frame to be received from either network with the next valid sequence number is accepted and passed up the stack to the receiving partition.
rules.test_hint: Send duplicate frames with same sequence number to test if second frame is discarded

rules.name: Duplicate frame discard

constraint.value: when the second frame is received with this sequence number, it is simply discarded

rules.source_quote: When the second frame is received with this sequence number, it is simply discarded.
rules.test_hint: Send multiple frames with identical sequence numbers to verify only first is processed

rules.name: Sequence number addition requirement
rules.source_quote: Per VL, the End System should add a sequence number for each transmitted frame on the AFDX network.
rules.test_hint: Send frames without sequence numbers to test if they are rejected

rules.name: Sequence number length
rules.source_quote: The frame sequence number should be one octet long with a range of 0 to 255.
rules.test_hint: Use sequence numbers longer than 1 octet to test field validation

rules.name: Sequence number value range
rules.source_quote: The frame sequence number should be one octet long with a range of 0 to 255.
rules.test_hint: Use sequence numbers outside 0-255 range to test validation

rules.name: Initial sequence number value
rules.source_quote: For each VL, the sequence number should initially be set to 0.
rules.test_hint: Start transmission with non-zero sequence number to test initial value enforcement

rules.name: Reset sequence number value
rules.source_quote: The sequence number is always assigned this initial value following a reset of the transmitting ES.
rules.test_hint: After simulated reset, start with non-zero sequence number to test reset behavior

rules.name: Sequence number increment
rules.source_quote: The frame sequence number should be incremented by one for each consecutive frame of the same VL
rules.test_hint: Increment sequence numbers by values other than 1 to test increment validation

rules.name: Sequence number wraparound behavior

constraint.value: wrap-around to 1 following the value 255

rules.source_quote: The frame sequence number should be incremented by one for each consecutive frame of the same VL and wrap-around to 1 following the value 255.
rules.test_hint: Send sequence number 255 followed by value other than 1 to test wraparound enforcement

rules.name: sequence number location in frame

constraint.value: sequence number must be located just before the MAC CRC field as part of the MAC payload

rules.source_quote: The frame sequence number should be located just before the MAC CRC field, as part of the MAC payload, as illustrated in Figure 3-19.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with sequence numbers placed in incorrect locations within the frame structure

rules.name: maximum time difference between redundant frames
rules.source_quote: In order to simplify the algorithm on the receiving End System, redundant copies of a frame should be sent within a maximum time difference of 0.5 ms.
rules.test_hint: Send redundant frames with time differences exceeding 0.5 ms between network A and B

rules.name: sequence number interval validation

constraint.value: [PSN+1, PSN+2] where PSN is previous sequence number with wraparound

rules.source_quote: For each network the Integrity Checking tests each frame for a sequence number in the interval: [PSN"+"1,PSN"+"2] Where Previous Sequence Number (PSN) is the sequence number of the previous frame received (but not necessarily forwarded) on this VL.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with sequence numbers outside the valid range [PSN+1, PSN+2]

rules.name: sequence number wraparound calculation

constraint.value: wraparound from 254: PSN+1=255, PSN+2=1 (wraps at 256)

rules.source_quote: The operator "+" takes the wrap-around of Sequence Numbers into account. So, for example if PSN = 254 then PSN"+"1= 255 and PSN"+"2 = 1.
rules.test_hint: Test sequence number validation across wraparound boundaries (e.g., 255 -> 0 -> 1)

rules.name: sequence number zero acceptance
rules.source_quote: The Integrity Checking should also accept the frame as valid in the following special cases: • The Received Sequence Number (RSN) is equal to 0
rules.test_hint: Send frames with sequence number 0 and verify they are accepted regardless of previous sequence number

rules.name: first frame after reset acceptance
rules.source_quote: The Integrity Checking should also accept the frame as valid in the following special cases: • The frame is the first frame received after any reset of the receiving ES
rules.test_hint: Test that the first frame after receiver reset is accepted regardless of sequence number

rules.name: invalid frame discard rule

constraint.value: frames not meeting sequence number criteria must be discarded

rules.source_quote: Frames that do not meet these criteria are discarded.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with invalid sequence numbers and verify they are discarded by the receiving end system

rules.name: sequence number zero transmission after reset

constraint.value: sequence number 0 is transmitted only after reset of transmitting equipment

rules.source_quote: The sequence number 0 is transmitted only after a reset of the transmitting equipment.
rules.test_hint: Send sequence number 0 frames without preceding reset condition and verify proper handling

rules.name: integrity checking disable capability
rules.source_quote: It should be possible on a per VL basis to disable the integrity checking on both networks through the configuration table. Disabling Integrity Checking allows the receiver to accept all frames from both Networks, A and B.
rules.test_hint: Test that when integrity checking is disabled, all frames are accepted regardless of sequence number validity

rules.name: skew max parameter configuration

constraint.value: maximum time between reception of two redundant frames, configured per VL

rules.source_quote: RM configuration is generally based on the SkewMax parameter: i.e. the maximum time between the reception of two redundant frames. This value depends on the network topology (number of switches crossed by the frames) and should be provided by the system integrator. The SkewMax value (expressed in ms) is given by configuration per VL
rules.test_hint: Send redundant frames with time differences exceeding the configured SkewMax value for a VL

rules.name: per VL network transmission configuration
rules.source_quote: On a per VL basis, the ES should be able to send messages on either or both networks. This property should be configurable.
rules.test_hint: Configure VL for single network transmission and verify frames are not sent on the other network

rules.name: per VL reception mode configuration
rules.source_quote: On a per VL basis, the ES should be able to receive: • A redundant VL and deliver to the partition one of the redundant data (RM active) • A redundant VL and deliver to the partition both redundant data (RM not active) • A non redundant VL on either interface and submit data from it to the partition (in this case, RM can be active or not)
rules.test_hint: Configure different reception modes and verify correct data delivery behavior to partitions

rules.name: First Win Frame Selection

constraint.value: deliver first of redundant frames received

rules.source_quote: When redundancy management is active, it should deliver the first of the redundant frames received.
rules.test_hint: Send duplicate frames on both redundant networks with different arrival times and verify only the first arriving frame is delivered

rules.name: Reset Persistence of First Win

constraint.value: first win property must persist across equipment resets

rules.source_quote: Reset of any equipment involved in the communication (transmitting End system, receiving End system or the AFDX switch) should not affect this property.
rules.test_hint: Trigger equipment resets during redundant frame transmission and verify first win behavior is maintained

rules.name: RSN-Only Frame Validation

constraint.value: use only RSN for frame rejection or acceptance

rules.source_quote: The Redundancy Management Algorithm should only use the RSN of a frame as the criterion for rejection or acceptance.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with corrupted payload but valid RSN sequence and verify they are accepted based solely on RSN

rules.name: Increasing RSN Order Forwarding

constraint.value: forward frames in increasing RSN order

rules.source_quote: For each VL at the receiver, the Redundancy Management (RM) function should ensure that frames are forwarded in an increasing RSN order.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with decreasing or random RSN values and verify only increasing sequence frames are forwarded

rules.name: Post-Skew RSN Reset

constraint.value: accept next frame with any sequence number after skew max exceeded

rules.source_quote: If skew max is exceeded after the reception of a frame, RM will accept the next frame whatever its sequence number is.
rules.test_hint: Trigger skew max condition then send frame with arbitrary RSN and verify it is accepted regardless of sequence

rules.name: In-Sequence Only Forwarding

constraint.value: forward only in-sequence frames without reordering

rules.source_quote: The Redundancy Management function must forward only in-sequence frames, but reordering is not required.
rules.test_hint: Send out-of-sequence frames and verify they are dropped, with no attempt to reorder and forward later

rules.name: Port Unidirectional Configuration
rules.source_quote: A user port is configured to either transmit or receive, but not both.
rules.test_hint: Configure a port for both transmit and receive simultaneously and verify the network rejects this configuration

rules.name: Sampling Message Size Constraint

constraint.value: <=VL_payload_size

rules.source_quote: Sampling Com Ports should not use IP fragmentation, therefore the size of each sampling message should be less than or equal to the payload size of the associated Virtual Link.
rules.test_hint: Send a sampling message larger than the VL payload size and verify it is rejected or causes an error

rules.name: Sampling Service Communication Pattern
rules.source_quote: Sampling service should be based on multicast and unidirectional communication to send data from one source to one or several receptors.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to use sampling service with bidirectional or unicast communication and verify it is not supported

rules.name: Sampling Service No Acknowledgment
rules.source_quote: The sampling service is simple, connectionless without acknowledge.
rules.test_hint: Send a sampling message and verify no acknowledgment is generated or expected

rules.name: Multiple Partition Access to Sampling Port
rules.source_quote: The last message stored in a particular sampling port should be able to be read by several partitions (i.e. several partitions may subscribe to this sampling port).
rules.test_hint: Configure multiple partitions to read from the same sampling port and verify all can access the latest message

rules.name: Freshness Indication Requirement
rules.source_quote: A freshness indication should be associated to each sampling port. This freshness indication should be available to each partition reading the message.
rules.test_hint: Read from a sampling port and verify freshness indication is provided and accessible to all reading partitions

rules.name: FIFO Message Ordering
rules.source_quote: To guarantee the sequence of messages, the queuing service should manage the messages with FIFO discipline in transmission and reception.
rules.test_hint: Send multiple messages through queuing service and verify they are received in the same order (FIFO)

rules.name: Queuing Service Maximum Data Size
rules.source_quote: Each instance of Queuing Service should be able to manage up to 8 k octets of application data (IP fragmentation is thus needed).
rules.test_hint: Send a queuing message larger than 8192 octets and verify it is rejected or causes an error

rules.name: Fragment Transmission Order

constraint.value: fragments_transmitted_in_order

rules.source_quote: When fragmentation is used, the fragments should be transmitted in-order to the AFDX network.
rules.test_hint: Send a fragmented message and verify fragments are transmitted to the network in the correct order

rules.name: Transmission Buffer Overflow Handling

constraint.value: send_error_indication_and_discard_frame

rules.source_quote: If a buffer overflow occurs in transmission, an error indication should be sent to the transmitting partition and the frame should be discarded
rules.test_hint: Cause a transmission buffer overflow and verify an error indication is sent and the frame is discarded

rules.name: Complete reassembly requirement

constraint.value: no data presented to partition until whole message reassembled

rules.source_quote: In case of fragmentation, no data should be presented to a partition in the queuing services FIFO until whole message has been reassembled.
rules.test_hint: Send fragmented packets and verify partial data is not delivered before all fragments arrive

rules.name: RX buffer overflow handling

constraint.value: send error message to partition and discard frame on overflow

rules.source_quote: If a buffer overflow occurs in reception, an error message should be sent to the receiving partition and the frame should be discarded.
rules.test_hint: Fill receive buffers to capacity and verify overflow frames are discarded with error indication

rules.name: UDP payload size limit
rules.source_quote: Each instance of the UDP Service Access Point should handle up to 8k octets.
rules.test_hint: Send UDP packets larger than 8192 octets and verify they are rejected or truncated

rules.name: SAP port buffer overflow handling

constraint.value: send error message to partition and discard frame on overflow

rules.source_quote: If receiver buffer overflow occurs, an error message is sent to the receiving partition, and the frame should be discarded.
rules.test_hint: Flood SAP port buffers to cause overflow and verify frames are discarded with error indication

rules.name: TFTP block size limit
rules.source_quote: Each instance of File Transfer service should be able to manage up to 8 k octets blocks.
rules.test_hint: Send TFTP blocks larger than 8192 octets and verify they are rejected or fragmented

rules.name: Maximum Sub-VL queues per VL
rules.source_quote: A VL FIFO queue should be able to manage at most 4 Sub-VL FIFO queues.
rules.test_hint: Configure more than 4 Sub-VL queues per VL and verify the configuration is rejected

rules.name: Round-robin Sub-VL scheduling

constraint.value: read Sub-VL queues in round-robin sequence, one frame per BAG

rules.source_quote: Each Sub-VF FIFO queue should be read in round-robin sequence such that if any Sub-VF FIFO queue has traffic, one frame per BAG is sent to the main VL.
rules.test_hint: Monitor frame ordering from multiple Sub-VLs to verify round-robin scheduling is enforced

rules.name: BAG boundary scheduling halt

constraint.value: halt sequence until BAG ends, restart with next Sub-VL queue

rules.source_quote: Once a frame is sent, the sequence is halted until the BAG ends and the sequence is then restarted with the next Sub-VF FIFO queue.
rules.test_hint: Verify that Sub-VL round-robin scheduling respects BAG boundaries and doesn't send multiple frames from same Sub-VL within one BAG

rules.name: Sub-VL queue exclusivity

constraint.value: Sub-VL FIFO queue read by only one VL FIFO queue

rules.source_quote: A Sub-VL FIFO queue should only be read by one VL FIFO queue.
rules.test_hint: Configure multiple VL queues to read from the same Sub-VL queue and verify the configuration is rejected

rules.name: Fragment-aware round-robin

constraint.value: round robin continues with fragmentation, one fragment per Sub-VL turn

rules.source_quote: The round robin continues in the presence of IP fragmentation so that one fragment is fetched from one Sub-VL, and then a frame or fragment is taken from the following Sub-VL.
rules.test_hint: Send fragmented packets through Sub-VLs and verify round-robin continues at fragment level, not complete packet level

rules.name: Ethernet frame IEEE 802.3 compliance

constraint.value: must_be_ieee_802_3_compliant

rules.source_quote: Any Ethernet Frame generated by the End System should be compliant with IEEE 802.3 standard.
rules.test_hint: Generate malformed Ethernet frames that violate IEEE 802.3 format requirements (invalid preamble, incorrect frame structure, etc.)

rules.name: Continuous transmission on link failure

constraint.value: continue_transmitting_on_physical_failure

rules.source_quote: All output interfaces will continue to transmit, even in the case of a physical layer link failure.
rules.test_hint: Simulate physical layer link failures and verify that End System continues attempting transmission instead of buffering frames

rules.name: Frame forwarding criteria

constraint.value: forward_if_valid_format_and_fcs_and_crc

rules.source_quote: In reception, if the AFDX frame format and Frame Check Sequence (FCS) and Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) are valid (without preamble and Start Frame Delimiter fields) the frame should be forwarded to the upper layer.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with corrupted FCS or CRC values and verify they are not forwarded to upper layers

rules.name: IPv4 version requirement
rules.source_quote: The packet structure version should be IPv4.
rules.test_hint: Send packets with IPv6 headers or invalid version field values (not 4) and verify rejection

rules.name: AFDX IPv4 total length range
rules.source_quote: Ordinarily, in the IPv4 packet structure, the Total Length field should range from 21 to 1500 bytes. In AFDX, this range is from 21 to 1499 due to the Sequence Number
rules.test_hint: Send IPv4 packets with Total Length values outside the 21-1499 byte range (e.g., 20 bytes or 1500 bytes) and verify rejection

rules.name: Unique data flow identification

constraint.value: unique_by_udp_tcp_port_ip_address_mac_address_physical_connection

rules.source_quote: A data flow is uniquely identified within AFDX network by the set of UDP/TCP destination port, IP destination address, MAC destination address and the physical Ethernet connection(s) of the receiving ES.
rules.test_hint: Create multiple data flows with identical addressing tuples and verify the network can distinguish them only if they differ in at least one of the four identifying elements

rules.name: Frame filtering based on addresses

constraint.value: filter_by_destination_addresses_and_physical_connections

rules.source_quote: Frame based filtering is done such that the receiving End System will only forward valid frames to a communication or a SAP port. Valid frame being defined by analysis of destination (TCP/UDP, IP, MAC) addresses and physical Ethernet connections.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with incorrect destination addresses (UDP/TCP port, IP, or MAC) to verify they are filtered out and not forwarded to communication/SAP ports

rules.name: Receiver Demultiplexing Based on Destination Addresses

constraint.value: demultiplexing is based only on the MAC, IP, UDP destination address

rules.source_quote: At the receiver, the demultiplexing is based only on the MAC, IP, UDP destination address.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with same destination addresses but different source addresses to verify receiver only uses destination fields for demultiplexing

rules.name: MAC Address Types
rules.source_quote: MAC address should be understood as potentially unicast or multicast Ethernet address.
rules.test_hint: Test network behavior with both unicast and multicast MAC addresses to verify proper handling of each type

rules.name: Unique Message Identification Quintuplet

constraint.value: UDP Source Port + Source IP + Destination MAC (VL identification) + Destination IP + UDP Destination Port provides unique identification for each message

rules.source_quote: Peer-to-peer communications are identified in each frame by UDP Source Port + Source IP + Destination MAC (VL identification) + Destination IP + UDP Destination Port... In the AFDX network, this quintuplet provides a unique identification for each message.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with identical quintuplets to verify network treats them as the same message, or send frames with different quintuplets to verify they are treated as different messages

rules.name: Multiple Source UDP Ports per Source IP

constraint.value: For a source IP, there should be several source UDP/TCP ports

rules.source_quote: For a source IP, there should be several source UDP/TCP ports.
rules.test_hint: Test with single source IP using multiple UDP source ports to verify proper multiplexing behavior

rules.name: Multiple Destination UDP Ports per Destination IP

constraint.value: For a destination IP there should be several destination UDP/TCP ports

rules.source_quote: For a destination IP there should be several destination UDP/TCP ports.
rules.test_hint: Test with single destination IP using multiple UDP destination ports to verify proper demultiplexing behavior

rules.name: Static Addressing for Intra-AFDX Communication

constraint.value: for each message, the addressing is statically defined

rules.source_quote: The principal characteristic of Intra-AFDX communication is the fact that for each message, the addressing is statically defined.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with dynamically changed addressing to verify network rejects or mishandles them compared to statically defined addresses

rules.name: AFDX Port Service Types
rules.source_quote: AFDX communication ports are characterised by the Sampling and the Queuing services.
rules.test_hint: Test port behavior with both sampling and queuing service configurations to verify different data handling behaviors

rules.name: SAP Port Bidirectional Communication Requirement

constraint.value: To obtain a bi-directional communication, two SAPs should be used (e.g.: SAP 30 000 Tx and SAP 30 000 Rx)

rules.source_quote: To obtain a bi-directional communication, two SAPs should be used (e.g.: SAP 30 000 Tx and SAP 30 000 Rx).
rules.test_hint: Test bidirectional communication with single SAP to verify it fails or behaves incorrectly compared to using two SAPs

rules.name: AFDX Port Bidirectional Communication Requirement

constraint.value: Bi-directional communication, at a single ES should require two AFDX communication ports : one transmitter and one receiver

rules.source_quote: Bi-directional communication, at a single ES should require two AFDX communication ports : one transmitter and one receiver, (e.g.: AFDX Com port 15 000 Tx and AFDX Com port 15 000 Rx).
rules.test_hint: Test bidirectional communication with single AFDX port to verify it fails or behaves incorrectly compared to using separate transmitter and receiver ports

rules.name: Bidirectional Communication Queuing Mode Requirement
rules.source_quote: For a bi-directional communication, the ports should be used in queuing mode.
rules.test_hint: Test bidirectional communication using sampling mode to verify it fails or behaves incorrectly compared to queuing mode

rules.name: IP Source Address Class A Private Format

constraint.value: Class A private address with first 8 bits '00001010'

rules.source_quote: The IP address should be Class A and private Internet Unicast Address (First 8 bits should be '0000 1010').
rules.test_hint: Send frames with IP source addresses that don't match the Class A private format (e.g., Class B, Class C, or non-private addresses)

rules.name: IP Address Spare Field Default Value
rules.source_quote: The Spare field is normally not used and set to zero as shown in Figure 3-37.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with non-zero values in the 3-bit spare field of the IP address

rules.name: IP Destination Address Format

value: IP Multicast address with Class D format

rules.source_quote: The IP destination address in the IP header of the AFDX frame should be: • Either the IP Unicast address to identify the target subscriber • Or an IP Multicast address compliant to the format shown in Figure 3-38
rules.test_hint: Send frames with IP destination addresses that are neither valid unicast nor properly formatted multicast addresses

rules.name: IP Multicast Address Class D Format

constraint.value: Class D with first 4 bits '1110'

rules.source_quote: Class D "1110" IP Multicast Identifier
rules.test_hint: Send frames with multicast addresses that don't have the proper Class D format (first 4 bits not '1110')

rules.name: IP Multicast Constant Field Value
rules.source_quote: Constant field 12 bits = "0000 1110 0000"
rules.test_hint: Send frames with multicast addresses having incorrect constant field values in the 12-bit constant field

rules.name: AFDX Communication Port Transmission Uniqueness

constraint.value: single quintuplet mapping per transmission port

rules.source_quote: In transmission, an AFDX Communication Port should only be linked to a single set UDP port source, IP source, VL (MAC destination), IP destination and UDP destination.
rules.test_hint: Configure a transmission AFDX Communication Port to map to multiple different quintuplets and observe if the system rejects the configuration or frames

rules.name: AFDX Communication Port Reception Uniqueness

constraint.value: single triplet mapping per reception port

rules.source_quote: In reception, an AFDX Communication Port should only be linked to a single set (unique UDP port destination, IP destination, VL (MAC destination)) and additionally to the Ethernet physical interface if the redundancy management is disabling.
rules.test_hint: Configure a reception AFDX Communication Port to receive from multiple different triplets (UDP port destination, IP destination, VL) and verify if the system enforces uniqueness

rules.name: Communication Port Unidirectional Access
rules.source_quote: Unidirectional access: Transmission (Tx) or reception (Rx)
rules.test_hint: Attempt to use a single AFDX Communication Port for both transmission and reception simultaneously

rules.name: SAP port transmission binding uniqueness

constraint.value: SAP Port must only be linked to a single set of (UDP port source, IP source, VL MAC destination)

rules.source_quote: In transmission, a SAP Port should only be linked to a single set (UDP port source, IP source and VL (MAC destination)).
rules.test_hint: Create multiple transmission bindings for the same SAP port with different UDP source ports, IP sources, or VL destinations

rules.name: SAP port reception binding uniqueness

constraint.value: SAP Port must only be linked to a single set of (UDP/TCP port destination, IP destination, VL MAC destination)

rules.source_quote: In reception, a SAP Port should only be linked to a single set (UDP/TCP port destination, IP destination and VL (MAC destination))
rules.test_hint: Create multiple reception bindings for the same SAP port with different UDP/TCP destination ports, IP destinations, or VL destinations

rules.name: Well-known port range allocation
rules.source_quote: 0 – 1023 Administered by ICANN "Well-known" port number
rules.test_hint: Use port numbers in well-known range for non-standard purposes or verify proper handling of well-known ports

rules.name: AFDX communication port range
rules.source_quote: AFDX Communication port AFDX → AFDX AFDX → Compliant network 1 024 – 65 535 Used for sampling and queuing communications
rules.test_hint: Use ports outside this range for AFDX communication or verify sampling/queuing communication restrictions

rules.name: Standard communication port range
rules.source_quote: AFDX → AFDX AFDX →Compliant network 0 – 1023 Used for standard communications e.g Port 69 to open a TFTP, Data loading (ARINC 615A), SNMP, etc..
rules.test_hint: Use well-known ports for non-standard communications or verify protocol-specific port usage

rules.name: SAP bidirectional communication port range
rules.source_quote: SAP AFDX → AFDX AFDX →Compliant network 1 024 – 65 535 Used for bi-directional communication: specific TFTP etc..
rules.test_hint: Use ports outside this range for bidirectional SAP communication or test bidirectional communication constraints

rules.name: Port number uniqueness within Virtual Link

constraint.value: Two identical port numbers cannot be used within a Virtual Link

rules.source_quote: the only technical limitation regarding port number duplication is that two identical port number cannot be used with in a Virtual Link
rules.test_hint: Configure multiple endpoints within the same Virtual Link to use identical port numbers

rules.name: Frame filtering stages

constraint.value: Frames must be filtered through rules about frame integrity, frame length, traffic budget and acceptable destinations

rules.source_quote: All frames arrive at the switch in the Filtering & Policing function stage where they are filtered in various steps that apply rules about frame integrity, frame length, traffic budget and acceptable destination(s)
rules.test_hint: Send frames that violate frame integrity, exceed length limits, exceed traffic budgets, or have unacceptable destinations

rules.name: Maximum frame size for Virtual Link
rules.source_quote: The maximum frame size for VLi is denoted S i max (expressed in bytes). S i max is a configurable parameter that should be in the range [84, 1538]
rules.test_hint: Send frames on a VL with frame size outside the configured S_i_max range

rules.name: Minimum frame size for Virtual Link
rules.source_quote: The minimum frame size for VLi is denoted S i min (expressed in bytes). S i min is a configurable parameter that should be in the range [84, 1538]
rules.test_hint: Configure S_i_min outside the valid range or send frames smaller than configured S_i_min

rules.name: Minimum frame size must not exceed maximum frame size

constraint.value: S_i_min <= S_i_max

rules.source_quote: S i min should be less than or equal to S i max
rules.test_hint: Configure S_i_min greater than S_i_max for a Virtual Link

rules.name: Ethernet frame includes IFG, Preamble, SFD and MAC frame

constraint.value: IFG(12) + Preamble(7) + SFD(1) + MAC_Frame(64-1518)

rules.source_quote: all fields have to be taken into account: IFG (12 octets) + Preamble (7 octets) + SFD (1 octet) + MAC Frame size (L = 64 to 1518 octets)
rules.test_hint: Generate frames missing required fields or with incorrect field sizes

rules.name: Frame Check Sequence must match calculated value

constraint.value: FCS_embedded == FCS_calculated

rules.source_quote: The frame integrity: whether the FCS embedded in the frame matches the calculation upon reception
rules.test_hint: Send frames with corrupted or incorrect FCS values

rules.name: Destination address must correspond to valid Virtual Link

constraint.value: destination_address_maps_to_valid_VL

rules.source_quote: Destination address validity (Ethernet Address corresponds to a valid VL, including constant field)
rules.test_hint: Send frames with destination addresses that don't map to configured Virtual Links

rules.name: Virtual Link must be valid for destination port

constraint.value: VL_permitted_on_destination_port

rules.source_quote: This VL is valid to be received on that destination port (according to the switch configuration table)
rules.test_hint: Send frames on ports where the Virtual Link is not configured to be received

rules.name: Ethernet frame size must be integral number of octets

constraint.value: frame_size_is_integral_octets

rules.source_quote: Ethernet frame size (L) is an integral number of octets (alignment)
rules.test_hint: Send frames with non-integral octet sizes (partial bytes)

rules.name: Ethernet frame size must not exceed Virtual Link maximum

constraint.value: L <= Lmax

rules.source_quote: Ethernet frame size (L) less that or equal to Lmax
rules.test_hint: Send frames larger than the configured Lmax for the Virtual Link

rules.name: Ethernet frame size must meet Virtual Link minimum for byte-based policing

constraint.value: S >= Smin

rules.source_quote: Ethernet frame size (S) greater than or equal to Smin, only in case where byte-based traffic policing is used
rules.test_hint: When byte-based policing is enabled, send frames smaller than Smin for the Virtual Link

rules.name: Non-compliant frames must be discarded and MIB updated

constraint.value: discard_frame_and_update_MIB

rules.source_quote: If the frame properties do not comply with the configuration parameters, the frame is filtered i.e. discarded, and one or more MIB entries updated
rules.test_hint: Send non-compliant frames and verify they are discarded and MIB counters are incremented

rules.name: Initial AC account setting

constraint.value: AC_i = S_i_max

rules.source_quote: Initially, the ACcount for VLi (also called ACi, expressed in bytes) is set to

rules.name: AC account crediting rate limit

constraint.value: upper_limit = BAG_i

rules.source_quote: ACi is credited as time elapses, proportionally to S i max with an upper limit of BAG i

rules.name: Ethernet frame total size calculation
rules.source_quote: Let s be the total Ethernet line size of the received frame (S = Ethernet frame size (L) + 20 octets; the 20 octets correspond to IFG+Preamble+SFD).
rules.test_hint: Generate frames and verify switch calculates total size correctly including 20-octet overhead

rules.name: Byte-based frame acceptance condition

constraint.value: if Byte_ACi > S then accept_frame and debit_Byte_ACi_by_S

rules.source_quote: If Byte ACi is greater than S, the frame is accepted and Byte ACi is debited by S
rules.test_hint: Send frames when byte account is exactly equal to or slightly less than frame size to test boundary conditions

rules.name: Byte-based frame rejection condition

constraint.value: if Byte_ACi < S then discard_frame and update_MIB and no_change_to_Byte_ACi

rules.source_quote: If Byte ACi is less than S, the frame is discarded, the appropriate MIB entry is updated and Byte ACi is not changed
rules.test_hint: Send frames when byte account is insufficient and verify frame is discarded and MIB is updated

rules.name: Frame-based frame acceptance condition

constraint.value: if Frame_ACi > S_i_max then accept_frame and debit_Frame_ACi_by_S_i_max

rules.source_quote: If Frame ACi is greater than S i max, the frame is accepted and Frame ACi is debited by S i max
rules.test_hint: Send frames when frame account is exactly equal to or slightly less than S_i_max to test boundary conditions

rules.name: Frame-based frame rejection condition

constraint.value: if Frame_ACi < S_i_max then discard_frame and update_MIB and no_change_to_Frame_ACi

rules.source_quote: If Frame ACi is less than S i max, the frame is discarded, the appropriate MIB entry is updated and Frame ACi is not changed
rules.test_hint: Send frames when frame account is insufficient and verify frame is discarded and MIB is updated

rules.name: Budget consumption exclusion for invalid frames

constraint.value: no_budget_consumed_for_discarded_frames

rules.source_quote: Budget Accounts (Bytes ACi and Frame ACi) should not be consumed by invalid frames, i.e. frames not forwarded by the forwarding function. No budget should be consumed by frames that are discarded by the filtering mechanisms.
rules.test_hint: Send invalid frames that get discarded and verify budget accounts are not debited

rules.name: Frame Check Sequence validation requirement

constraint.value: test_frame_with_CRC_and_discard_if_corrupted

rules.source_quote: In order to guarantee total network robustness, it is important that only uncorrupted frames be forwarded. Therefore, upon arrival, the switch should test each frame by use of the Frame Check Sequence (CRC) field according to IEEE Std 802.3. The Switch should discard Frames that do not satisfy this test.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with corrupted CRC values and verify they are discarded by the switch

rules.name: Ethernet frame size upper limit
rules.source_quote: The switch should discard incoming Ethernet frames having an Ethernet frame size (L) greater than 1518 or less than 64 bytes.
rules.test_hint: Send frames larger than 1518 bytes and verify they are discarded

rules.name: Ethernet frame size lower limit
rules.source_quote: The switch should discard incoming Ethernet frames having an Ethernet frame size (L) greater than 1518 or less than 64 bytes.
rules.test_hint: Send frames smaller than 64 bytes and verify they are discarded

rules.name: Frame Size Alignment
rules.source_quote: The switch should discard incoming frames having an Ethernet frame size that is not an integral number of octets (alignment errors).
rules.test_hint: Send a frame with a non-integral number of octets (e.g., fractional bits)

rules.name: Maximum Frame Size Enforcement

constraint.value: frame_size <= VL_Lmax

rules.source_quote: The switch should discard incoming frames which total Ethernet line size is greater than the maximum size (Lmax) allowed for the relevant VL, as such a frame would consume more bandwidth than allocated.
rules.test_hint: Send a frame with size exceeding the configured Lmax for its VL

rules.name: Minimum Frame Size Enforcement (Byte-based Policing)

constraint.value: frame_size >= VL_Smin (when byte-based policing enabled)

rules.source_quote: In the case where byte-based policing is used, the switch should also discard incoming frames which total Ethernet line size is smaller than the minimum size (Smin) allowed for the relevant VL.
rules.test_hint: When byte-based policing is enabled, send a frame smaller than the configured Smin for its VL

rules.name: MAC Destination Address Constant Field Validation

constraint.value: 32-bit constant field in MAC destination address must be correct

rules.source_quote: The switch should discard incoming frames with a MAC destination address that has an erroneous 32-bit constant field.
rules.test_hint: Send a frame with an incorrect 32-bit constant field in the MAC destination address

rules.name: VL Port Authorization

constraint.value: VL id must be authorized for the incoming port

rules.source_quote: The switch should discard incoming frames for which the VL id is not allowed on the incoming port.
rules.test_hint: Send a frame with a VL ID that is not configured as allowed on the incoming port

rules.name: BAG Value Range
rules.source_quote: The Traffic Policing function of the Switch should at least be configurable for BAG values in the range 1ms to 128 ms.
rules.test_hint: Configure a VL with BAG values outside the range 1-128ms

rules.name: Maximum Jitter Value Range
rules.source_quote: The traffic policing function should at a minimum be configurable for maximum allowed Jitter values in the range 0 to 10 milliseconds.
rules.test_hint: Configure a VL with jitter values outside the range 0-10ms

rules.name: Ethernet Frame Size Range
rules.source_quote: The traffic policing function should be able to handle at least Ethernet frames sizes (L) in the range [64-1518] octets.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with sizes outside the 64-1518 octet range

rules.name: Shared VL BAG Consistency

constraint.value: All VLs sharing one ACi must have the same BAG value

rules.source_quote: When one ACi is used by a group of VL, all the VL of this group should have the same BAG and the same minimum (smin) and maximum (smax) total Ethernet line size values.
rules.test_hint: Configure multiple VLs sharing an account with different BAG values

rules.name: Shared VL Frame Size Consistency

constraint.value: All VLs sharing one ACi must have the same Smin and Smax values

rules.source_quote: When one ACi is used by a group of VL, all the VL of this group should have the same BAG and the same minimum (smin) and maximum (smax) total Ethernet line size values.
rules.test_hint: Configure multiple VLs sharing an account with different Smin or Smax values

rules.name: Shared VL Jitter Maximum Selection

constraint.value: ACi jitter parameter = maximum of all VL jitter values in the group

rules.source_quote: When one ACi is used by a group of VLs, the traffic policing function should use the maximum of the jitter values of all of the VLs in the group as the jitter parameter for the ACi.
rules.test_hint: Configure VLs with different jitter values in a shared account and verify the maximum is used

rules.name: Traffic Policing Resolution
rules.source_quote: Traffic should be policed with a resolution of less than or equal to 100 μs.
rules.test_hint: Test timing precision of policing decisions with frame arrivals spaced closer than 100μs apart

rules.name: Traffic policing time granularity tolerance
rules.source_quote: Traffic should be policed with a relative tolerance on the resolution of ±10-4.
rules.test_hint: Generate traffic with very precise timing that exceeds the allowed tolerance for policing accuracy

rules.name: Virtual Link frame order preservation

constraint.value: input_order_equals_output_order

rules.source_quote: The order of input and output frames belonging to a Virtual Link should be maintained by the switch.
rules.test_hint: Send multiple frames on same VL and verify if switch reorders them during forwarding

rules.name: Frame Check Sequence preservation

constraint.value: no_modification_allowed

rules.source_quote: The switch should not modify the Frame Check Sequence of incoming frames.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with specific FCS values and verify switch does not regenerate or modify them

rules.name: CRC regeneration prohibition
rules.source_quote: the CRC may not be regenerated within the switch under any circumstance, including at re-transmission.
rules.test_hint: Force switch to retransmit frames and verify CRC remains unchanged from original

rules.name: Destination address based forwarding

constraint.value: use_destination_address_for_port_lookup

rules.source_quote: For each frame, the content of the Destination Address field should be used to obtain from the configuration table the appropriate port(s) to which the frame has to be forwarded.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with unknown or invalid destination addresses and verify forwarding behavior

rules.name: Frame discard on buffer congestion

constraint.value: discard_frame_on_congestion

rules.source_quote: If an output port cannot accept a frame due to buffer congestion, this frame should be discarded for this port.
rules.test_hint: Flood output port with traffic to cause buffer congestion and verify frame discard behavior

rules.name: Frame discard on link failure

constraint.value: discard_buffered_frames_on_link_failure

rules.source_quote: In the case of a link failure of a port, frames forwarded to and held in buffers of this port should be discarded for this port.
rules.test_hint: Simulate link failure on output port and verify buffered frames are discarded

rules.name: Maximum frame delay enforcement

constraint.value: discard_frames_exceeding_max_delay

rules.source_quote: An output port should not transmit frames that are older than "max delay." The "max delay" parameter is defined on a per port basis in the configuration table.
rules.test_hint: Delay frames in switch buffers beyond configured max_delay parameter and verify they are discarded

rules.name: Frame delay measurement definition

constraint.value: last_bit_arrival_to_last_bit_exit

rules.source_quote: The maximum delay parameter of a frame on a given port is defined as the maximum elapsed time between the two following events: • Arrival of the last bit of a frame on the input port of a switch • Exit of this last bit of the frame from the given output port of the switch
rules.test_hint: Measure actual frame delays and compare against the defined measurement points

rules.name: Any port to any port forwarding

constraint.value: any_input_to_any_output_combination

rules.source_quote: The switch should have the capability to receive a frame on any port and forward it to any combination of ports (including the receiving port).
rules.test_hint: Test forwarding frames to all possible port combinations including loopback to receiving port

rules.name: Two traffic priority classes
rules.source_quote: The Switch should have a traffic prioritization mechanism based on MAC destination address with 2 traffic classes: High Priority and Low Priority.
rules.test_hint: Send traffic with invalid priority levels or test priority handling with frames assigned to undefined classes

rules.name: High priority frame transmission precedence

constraint.value: high_priority_before_low_priority

rules.source_quote: For each output port, frames with a priority set to high should be sent prior to the one set to low.
rules.test_hint: Queue low priority frames then send high priority frames to verify scheduling order

rules.name: No frame preemption during transmission
rules.source_quote: A low priority frame in the process of being transmitted should not be pre-empted by the arrival of a high priority frame.
rules.test_hint: Start transmitting low priority frame then send high priority frame to verify no preemption occurs

rules.name: Minimum Inter Frame Gap enforcement

constraint.value: minimum_gap_between_frames

rules.source_quote: If frames are present at the output port, switch should send them with a minimum Inter Frame Gap.
rules.test_hint: Monitor frame transmission timing to verify minimum inter-frame gap is maintained

rules.name: MIB variable update frequency
rules.source_quote: The Fault/Healthy MIB variable should be updated every 100 ms (like the other MIB variables).
rules.test_hint: Generate SNMP requests at intervals other than 100ms and verify if MIB updates are properly synchronized

rules.name: Fault/Healthy indicator update frequency
rules.source_quote: The update of the Fault/Healthy indicator output should be performed at least every 100 ms.
rules.test_hint: Monitor fault indicator updates and verify they occur at minimum 100ms intervals, test with faster update requests

rules.name: Fault indicator trigger condition

constraint.value: set to Fault when at least one used Ethernet port is in fault

rules.source_quote: The Healthy/Fault indicator should be set to "Fault" when at least one used Ethernet port is in fault.
rules.test_hint: Simulate port faults on different Ethernet ports and verify fault indicator triggers correctly for any single port failure

rules.name: Configuration file selection exclusivity
rules.source_quote: Depending on the operating mode, the appropriate file is selected in an exclusive mode.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to load multiple configuration files simultaneously or switch between modes rapidly to test exclusivity enforcement

rules.name: Network-wide configuration file identity

constraint.value: all files have to be identical for all switches within a network

rules.source_quote: All files have to be identical for all switches within a network.
rules.test_hint: Load different configuration files on different switches in the same network and observe network behavior inconsistencies

rules.name: Default configuration usage condition

constraint.value: used when Switch is empty or in Dataloading mode

rules.source_quote: The Default_Configuration_File, corresponding to the resident configuration, that is used when the Switch is empty (no field loadable software yet loaded) or when the Switch is being dataloaded (in both case, the Switch is in Dataloading mode (DL))
rules.test_hint: Force switch into different states and verify correct configuration file is selected based on operating mode

rules.name: OPS configuration usage condition

constraint.value: used when Switch is in Operational mode

rules.source_quote: The OPS_Configuration_File, corresponding to the loadable configuration, that is used when the Switch is in Operational mode (OPS)
rules.test_hint: Attempt to use OPS configuration while switch is in other modes and verify proper rejection or mode switching

rules.name: Default physical port number
rules.source_quote: Port # 1 is the default external physical port used to communicate with the End System of the Switch.
rules.test_hint: Test switch behavior when frames arrive on ports other than port 1 during default configuration state

rules.name: Default port speed
rules.source_quote: The default port speed should be set to 100 Mbps, without auto negotiation.
rules.test_hint: Test switch behavior when default port is configured to speeds other than 100 Mbps

rules.name: Auto negotiation disabled on default port
rules.source_quote: The default port speed should be set to 100 Mbps, without auto negotiation.
rules.test_hint: Test switch behavior when auto negotiation is enabled on the default port

rules.name: Switch subscribes to unique default reception VL

constraint.value: Each switch subscribes to exactly one unique reception VL based on position

rules.source_quote: Depending of its position in the aircraft network, acquired by pin programming, the Switch subscribes by default to one unique reception VL, further called VL (0, position).
rules.test_hint: Test switch behavior when configured with multiple default reception VLs or no default reception VL

rules.name: End System only processes frames with matching IP destination

constraint.value: Only accept frames where IP destination matches switch's own IP address

rules.source_quote: The End System Function of the Switch will only take into account the frames whose IP destination field corresponds to its own IP address, deduced from Pin Programming P 1 to P1 2
rules.test_hint: Send frames to the switch with IP destinations that don't match the switch's IP address

rules.name: Policing function activated on default VL

constraint.value: Policing function must be active on default VL according to configuration values

rules.source_quote: The policing function of the switch is activated on the default VL, according to the values defined in the configuration file.
rules.test_hint: Send traffic on default VL that exceeds the configured policing parameters (BAG, smax)

rules.name: Switch has unique default transmission VL

constraint.value: Each switch has exactly one unique transmission VL based on position

rules.source_quote: Each Switch has a unique default transmission VL, further called VL (1, position).
rules.test_hint: Test switch behavior when configured with multiple default transmission VLs

rules.name: Default transmission VL identifier format

constraint.value: 0000P1P2P3P4P5P6P7P8P9P10P11P12 where P1-P12 are pin programming values

rules.source_quote: 0 0 0 0 P1 P2P3P4P5P6P7P8P9P10P11P12 Figure 4-7 – Characteristics of the VL Identifier Where P1 to P12 correspond to the following pin programming values: 1 = GROUND and 0 = OPEN.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with VL identifiers that don't match the required format for default transmission VL

rules.name: Pin programming bit values
rules.source_quote: Where P1 to P12 correspond to the following pin programming values: 1 = GROUND and 0 = OPEN.

rules.name: Switch uses own IP and MAC as source addresses

constraint.value: IP and MAC source addresses must be the switch's own addresses derived from pin programming

rules.source_quote: When the End System of the Switch will send frame, the IP and MAC source addresses fields in the AFDX frame will be the own Switch IP and MAC addresses, deduced from Pin Programming P1 to P12
rules.test_hint: Monitor frames sent by switch to verify source addresses match expected values based on pin programming

rules.name: Same OPS configuration file for all switches

constraint.value: All switches in network must use same OPS_Configuration_File (same P/N)

rules.source_quote: The same OPS_Configuration_File (same P/N) is loaded in all the Switches of the Avionics Data Communications Network.
rules.test_hint: Load different OPS configuration files on different switches and test network behavior

rules.name: Switch accesses only position-specific configuration table

constraint.value: Switch only accesses the configuration table corresponding to its pin-programmed position

rules.source_quote: Depending of its current position, acquired by pin programming, the Switch only has access to the dedicated table of the OPS_Configuration_File.
rules.test_hint: Test switch behavior when trying to access configuration tables for different positions

rules.name: Maximum allowed total Ethernet line size per VL

constraint.value: configurable per VL

rules.source_quote: Maximum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (Smax)
rules.test_hint: Send frames on a VL that exceed the configured Smax value to test policing function

rules.name: Minimum allowed total Ethernet line size per VL

constraint.value: configurable per VL

rules.source_quote: Minimum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (Smin)
rules.test_hint: Send frames on a VL that are smaller than the configured Smin value to test policing function

rules.name: VL priority classification
rules.source_quote: Prioritization (high or low)
rules.test_hint: Test switch behavior by sending frames on VLs with different priority settings and verify scheduling/buffering behavior

rules.name: Port operational state
rules.source_quote: Port State (ON/ OFF)
rules.test_hint: Send frames to ports configured as OFF to verify they are not forwarded

rules.name: Output buffer size for low priority VLs

constraint.value: configurable per port

rules.source_quote: Output Buffer Size for Low Priority VLs
rules.test_hint: Send enough low priority traffic to overflow the output buffer and test buffer management behavior

rules.name: Output buffer size for high priority VLs

constraint.value: configurable per port

rules.source_quote: Output Buffer Size for High Priority VLs
rules.test_hint: Send enough high priority traffic to overflow the output buffer and test buffer management behavior

rules.name: Switch enters INIT mode after power rise or reset

constraint.value: switch must enter INIT mode after power rise or reset

rules.source_quote: The Switch enters the INIT mode after power rises or after a reset.
rules.test_hint: Test switch behavior immediately after simulated power cycle or reset to verify it enters INIT mode

rules.name: PASSIVE mode stops all functions except network management

constraint.value: only network management communication allowed, all other functions stopped

rules.source_quote: In PASSIVE MODE, the Switch only offers the capability to communicate with the Network Management Function), all others functions should be stopped.
rules.test_hint: When switch is in PASSIVE mode, verify that normal frame forwarding is stopped while network management remains accessible

rules.name: QUIET mode entry on catastrophic failure

constraint.value: enter QUIET mode on catastrophic failure that makes functional behavior questionable

rules.source_quote: QUIET mode is entered in the event of any sort of catastrophic failure that would cause the functional behavior of the switch to be questionable
rules.test_hint: Simulate catastrophic failures or corrupted configurations to verify switch enters QUIET mode and stops normal operation

rules.name: Fault indicator state during INIT mode

constraint.value: fault indicator must stay in fault state during INIT mode

rules.source_quote: During INIT, the Fault/Healthy indicator should stay in the Fault state.
rules.test_hint: Monitor fault indicator during switch initialization to verify it remains in fault state throughout INIT mode

rules.name: OPS mode entry conditions

constraint.value: Switch enters OPS mode only if compatibility checks are correct AND shop condition is not active

rules.source_quote: After the initialization sequence, the Switch should enter in OPS (operational mode) if the result of compatibility checks is correct and if the shop condition is not active.
rules.test_hint: Simulate switch with failed compatibility checks or active shop condition and verify it does not enter OPS mode

rules.name: OPS mode switch functions

constraint.value: In OPS mode, Switch must perform frames filtering, Traffic policing, Switching function, and End System function using OPS_Configuration_File data

rules.source_quote: In OPS, the Switch should perform its normal functions (frames filtering and Traffic policing functions, Switching function, End System function) exclusively relying upon the data contained in the activated part of the OPS_Configuration_File.
rules.test_hint: Verify switch only uses OPS_Configuration_File data and performs all required functions when in OPS mode

rules.name: DL mode entry from INIT conditions

constraint.value: From INIT mode, Switch enters DL mode only if Switch_Ground_Condition is active AND (compatibility checks incorrect OR no loaded software)

rules.source_quote: To allow the uploading of an empty Switch (it means with no loaded software, example: after the installation of an empty Switch in place of a failed one), from the INIT MODE, the Switch should enter in DL MODE only if the following conditions are both true: • The Switch_Ground_Condition is active • The results of compatibility checks are incorrect or there is no loaded software
rules.test_hint: Test switch behavior when ground condition is inactive or when compatibility checks are correct with loaded software

rules.name: DL mode entry from OPS conditions

constraint.value: From OPS mode, Switch enters DL mode only if Switch_Ground_Condition is active AND received ARINC 615A uploading initialization request AND header file accepted

rules.source_quote: From the OPS MODE, the Switch should enter the DL MODE only if the following conditions are all true: • The Switch_Ground_Condition is active • The Switch received an ARINC 615A uploading operation initialization request from the dataloader ([TH_Uploading_Initialization] message) addressed to the own end system of the Switch • The header file has been received and accepted
rules.test_hint: Test transition by sending malformed initialization requests or when ground condition is inactive

rules.name: DL mode configuration data source

constraint.value: In DL mode, Switch End System function must use only Default_Configuration_Table data

rules.source_quote: In DL Mode, the Switch should perform its End System function exclusively relying upon the data contained in its resident configuration table: Default_Configuration_Table.
