rules.test_hint: Verify switch only uses Default_Configuration_Table and not OPS_Configuration_File when in DL mode

rules.name: PASSIVE mode entry conditions

constraint.value: From INIT mode, Switch enters PASSIVE mode if pin programming parity check fails OR safety test result is incorrect

rules.source_quote: From the INIT mode, the Switch should enter in PASSIVE Mode as soon as one of the following conditions is true: • Pin programming parity check fails • Safety Test (if any) result is incorrect
rules.test_hint: Simulate pin programming parity failures or safety test failures and verify switch enters PASSIVE mode

rules.name: PASSIVE mode switch function restrictions

constraint.value: In PASSIVE mode, Switch functions must be stopped and switch must remain silent, except Network Management Function communication

rules.source_quote: In PASSIVE Mode, the functions of the Switch should be stopped and the switch should keep silent. Nevertheless, the capability to communicate with the Network Management Function should be maintained except if the passive state results from an erroneous parity of the pin programming discretes.
rules.test_hint: Verify switch does not perform normal switching functions but can still communicate with Network Management Function

rules.name: QUIET mode frame transmission restriction

constraint.value: In QUIET mode, switch functions are stopped, switch does not transmit frames, and all ports are disabled

rules.source_quote: In QUIET mode, the functions of the switch are stopped, the switch does not transmit frames or allow communication with the switch management function (SNMP). The switch software disables all ports when transitioning to QUIET mode.
rules.test_hint: Verify switch completely stops frame transmission and disables all ports when in QUIET mode

rules.name: QUIET mode entry conditions

value: Default OPS software CRC check failure
Default Configuration file CRC check failure

rules.source_quote: QUIET mode is entered in the event of any sort of catastrophic failure that would cause the functional behavior of the switch to be questionable. Some examples of these types are failures are: • Programming pin CRC failure • Heart Beat monitor test failure • Boot Code CRC failure • Processor Instruction test failure • Address/Data Bus monitor failure • RAM memory monitoring failure • Built-In-Self-Test (BIST) failure • Hardware register test failure • Default OPS software CRC check failure • Default Configuration file CRC check failure
rules.test_hint: Simulate any of these catastrophic failures and verify switch enters QUIET mode and stops all functions

rules.name: maximum_field_loadable_software_limit
rules.source_quote: The Switch should not have more than two field loadable software (OPS_Configuration_File and OPS_Software).

rules.name: pin_programming_read_condition

constraint.value: Hardware program pins should be read during initialization only if Switch_Ground_Condition is true

rules.source_quote: Hardware program pins should be read during the initialization (INIT mode) of the SWITCH only if the Switch_Ground_Condition is true and before performing the Safety Test (if any).
rules.test_hint: Test switch behavior when pin programming is attempted while Switch_Ground_Condition is false

rules.name: pin_programming_flight_behavior

constraint.value: When Switch_Ground_Condition is false, hardware program pins should not be read and switch should use last memorized values

rules.source_quote: When the Switch_Ground_Condition is false, hardware program pins should not be read. The Switch should use the last memorized values.
rules.test_hint: Verify switch ignores pin programming changes when Switch_Ground_Condition is false

rules.name: pin_programming_parity_check

constraint.value: The 12 program pins (P1 to P12) should be checked by a parity bit

rules.source_quote: The 12 program pins (P1 to P12) should be checked by a parity bit.
rules.test_hint: Send pin programming with invalid parity and verify switch rejects it

rules.name: pin_programming_count
rules.source_quote: The Switch should acquire its position in the aircraft with 12 pin programming, named P1 to P12.
rules.test_hint: Test switch behavior with fewer or more than 12 programming pins

rules.name: maximum_vl_processing_capacity
rules.source_quote: The filtering, policing, and forwarding function of the switch should be able to process at least 4096 VLs.
rules.test_hint: Send traffic with more than 4096 different VLs and verify switch can handle them

rules.name: port_speed_configuration
rules.source_quote: Each port speed should be configurable to operate to speeds of 10 Mbps or 100Mps in full duplex, without auto negotiation.
rules.test_hint: Configure ports to unsupported speeds and verify rejection

rules.name: full_duplex_requirement
rules.source_quote: Each port speed should be configurable to operate to speeds of 10 Mbps or 100Mps in full duplex, without auto negotiation.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to configure half-duplex mode and verify rejection

rules.name: auto_negotiation_prohibition
rules.source_quote: Each port speed should be configurable to operate to speeds of 10 Mbps or 100Mps in full duplex, without auto negotiation.
rules.test_hint: Enable auto-negotiation and verify it is not used or is rejected

rules.name: deterministic_processing_requirement

constraint.value: Given a deterministic configuration, switch must process all incoming frames at wire speed whatever their size

rules.source_quote: Given a deterministic configuration (a deterministic configuration is defined by the absence of any output port saturation) the switch must be able to process (i.e. receive, filter, police, relay, transmit) all frames that are incoming at wire speed whatever their size.
rules.test_hint: Send frames at wire speed with deterministic configuration and verify no drops

rules.name: mac_layer_receive_speed

constraint.value: MAC layer of each switch input port should receive frames at wire speed

rules.source_quote: The MAC layer of each switch input port should be able to receive frames at wire speed.
rules.test_hint: Send frames at maximum wire speed and verify MAC layer can receive them without drops

rules.name: filter_wire_speed_capability

constraint.value: Each switch port should filter frames of any valid size arriving at wire speed

rules.source_quote: Each switch port should be able to filter frames of any valid size that are arriving at wire speed.
rules.test_hint: Send frames of varying sizes at wire speed and verify filtering operates correctly

rules.name: police_wire_speed_capability

constraint.value: Each switch port should police VLs for frames of any valid size arriving at wire speed

rules.source_quote: Each switch port should be able to police the VLs for frames of any valid size that are arriving at wire speed
rules.test_hint: Send VL traffic of varying frame sizes at wire speed and verify policing functions correctly

rules.name: relay_wire_speed_capability

constraint.value: Given deterministic configuration, switch should relay all non-rejected incoming frames at wire speed whatever their size

rules.source_quote: Given a deterministic configuration, the switch should be able to relay all incoming frames that are not rejected by filtering and policing, at wire speed and whatever their size.
rules.test_hint: Send frames that pass filtering and policing at wire speed and verify relay operates without delays

rules.name: MAC layer wire speed transmission requirement

constraint.value: must transmit frames at wire speed

rules.source_quote: The MAC layer of each switch output port should be able to transmit frames at wire speed.
rules.test_hint: Generate continuous back-to-back frames at maximum rate and verify switch can maintain wire speed transmission without dropping or delaying frames

rules.name: Switch technological latency limit
rules.source_quote: The technological latency of the switch should be less than 100 μs.
rules.test_hint: Measure time between reception of last bit of input frame and transmission of last bit of output frame, verify it stays under 100 μs

rules.name: Minimum output port buffer capacity
rules.source_quote: Each output port of the switch should be able to buffer at least 512 frames (balanced between high and low priority).
rules.test_hint: Send more than 512 frames to a single output port simultaneously and verify the switch can buffer them without dropping frames

rules.name: Buffer allocation balance between priorities

constraint.value: balanced between high and low priority

rules.source_quote: Each output port of the switch should be able to buffer at least 512 frames (balanced between high and low priority).
rules.test_hint: Send mix of high and low priority frames exceeding buffer capacity and verify both priority levels get fair buffer allocation

rules.name: Performance measurement burst duration
rules.source_quote: The actual performance is measured by the time necessary to process all frames received during a 1 ms burst of back-to-back frames
rules.test_hint: Send burst of frames for exactly 1 ms duration and measure if end system can process all frames within specification

rules.name: Performance percentage calculation formula

constraint.value: 100 × (1 / processing_time) where processing_time = last_frame_latency - technological_latency + 1

rules.source_quote: Performance = 100 x 1 / (lastframelatency-technologicallatency+1) = 100 x 1 / processing_time
rules.test_hint: Measure actual latencies during burst test and verify calculated performance matches expected wire speed percentage

rules.name: Redundancy management disabled during performance test
rules.source_quote: The redundancy management algorithm is disabled.
rules.test_hint: During performance testing, verify that redundancy management is not active and both A and B network data are processed as separate VLs

rules.name: ethernet_big_endian_byte_order

constraint.value: integers must be sent with most significant byte first (Big Endian)

rules.source_quote: An aircraft data network for byte order, like the internet standard, specifies that integers are sent with the most significant byte first (i.e., Big Endian style).
rules.test_hint: Send frames with integers in little endian format to violate the big endian requirement

rules.name: packet_byte_ordering

constraint.value: most significant bytes appear nearest the beginning of packet, least significant bytes nearest the end

rules.source_quote: If one considers the successive bytes in a packet as it travels from one machine to another, a binary integer in that packet has its most significant bytes nearest the beginning of the packet and its least significant byte nearest the end of the packet.
rules.test_hint: Create packets with reversed byte ordering where least significant bytes appear before most significant bytes

rules.name: ethernet_memory_representation

constraint.value: data represented in memory with higher bit numbers and bytes first at lower address values

rules.source_quote: Ethernet is defined as being Big Endian. This means data is represented in memory with higher bit numbers and bytes first (lower address values) followed by the bytes containing lower bit numbers.
rules.test_hint: Generate frames with memory representation that violates big endian layout expectations

rules.name: data_element_definition

constraint.value: data element must be a specific value defined by range and resolution representing discrete information

rules.source_quote: A data element is a specific value, defined by range and resolution that represents a discrete piece of information.
rules.test_hint: Send data elements that exceed their defined range or resolution constraints

rules.name: Signed 32-bit integer range constraint
rules.source_quote: Signed_32 Integer 32 -2³¹ ... 2³¹ - 1
rules.test_hint: Send frames with Signed_32 values outside the range -2³¹ to 2³¹-1

rules.name: Signed 64-bit integer range constraint
rules.source_quote: Signed_64 Integer 64 -2⁶³ … 2⁶³ - 1
rules.test_hint: Send frames with Signed_64 values outside the range -2⁶³ to 2⁶³-1

rules.name: 32-bit floating point range constraint
rules.test_hint: Send frames with Float_32 values outside IEEE 754 single precision range

rules.name: 64-bit floating point range constraint
rules.test_hint: Send frames with Float_64 values outside IEEE 754 double precision range

rules.name: Boolean size constraint
rules.source_quote: Boolean 32 Not Applicable
rules.test_hint: Send frames with Boolean values not encoded as 32-bit fields

rules.name: Network-independent data type requirement

constraint.value: well-defined bit and byte order that enables applications to send and receive regardless of native bit or byte order of host processors

rules.source_quote: These data types have a well-defined bit and byte order that enables applications to send and receive a data element via the network regardless of the native bit or byte order of the host processors used in the system.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with incorrect byte order encoding for the defined primitive data types

rules.name: Signed 32-bit integer format compliance

constraint.value: 32-bit two's complement representation

rules.source_quote: The 32-bit signed integer uses the two's complement data representation format.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with signed integers not using two's complement format or with incorrect bit width

rules.name: Signed 64-bit integer format compliance

constraint.value: 64-bit two's complement representation

rules.source_quote: The 64-bit signed integer uses the two's complement data representation
rules.test_hint: Send frames with 64-bit signed integers not using two's complement format or with incorrect bit width

rules.name: 32-bit floating point IEEE 754 compliance

constraint.value: IEEE 754 single precision format with 1 sign bit, 8 exponent bits, 23 mantissa bits

rules.source_quote: The single precision floating point format is 32 bits long with 3 fields. These fields are: 1. S: sign bit – 0 indicates a positive number, 1 indicates a negative number. 2. E: exponent – base 2 number, 2 is raised to this power, 8 bits. 3. F: mantissa – the fractional part, base 2, 23 bits in representation.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with 32-bit floats that don't conform to IEEE 754 format or have incorrect field sizes

rules.name: 64-bit floating point IEEE 754 compliance

constraint.value: IEEE 754 double precision format with 1 sign bit, 11 exponent bits, 52 mantissa bits

rules.source_quote: The double precision floating point format is 64 bits long with 3 fields. These fields are: 1. S: sign bit – 0 indicates a positive number, 1 indicates a negative number. 2. E: exponent – base 2 number, 2 is raised to this power, 11 bits. 3. F: mantissa – the fractional part, base 2, 52 bits in representation.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with 64-bit floats that don't conform to IEEE 754 format or have incorrect field sizes

rules.name: Boolean representation in 32-bit field

constraint.value: Single bit in 32-bit field, using bit 0 (LSB), where 1=true and 0=false

rules.source_quote: Booleans are represented by a single bit in a 32-bit field. If just one Boolean is represented by a 32-bit field, bit 0 (least significant bit) is used. If bit 0 is a logical "1" the Boolean is said to be true (or yes, or active, or on, etc). If bit 0 is a logical "0" the value of the Boolean is said to be false (or no, or inactive, or off, etc.).
rules.test_hint: Send frames with boolean values not using bit 0 of a 32-bit field or using incorrect encoding

rules.name: No scaling factors for integer and floating point data
rules.source_quote: The integer and floating point data types are never scaled in AFDX messages. The scale factor is always one (1), in contrast to ARINC 429 where parameters quite often have scale factors associated with them other than 1.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with integer or floating point data that includes scaling factors other than 1

rules.name: Boolean bit assignment order

constraint.value: Booleans are assigned to a structure starting from the least significant bit and filling in toward the most significant bit

rules.source_quote: Booleans are assigned to a structure starting from the least significant bit and filling in toward the most significant bit.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with boolean data packed in wrong bit order (MSB to LSB instead of LSB to MSB)

rules.name: Unused bits must be zero

constraint.value: Unused bits at the most significant end of the 32-bit structure must be all binary zeros

rules.source_quote: Unused bits at the most significant end of the 32-bit structure must be all binary zeros.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with unused boolean bits set to 1 instead of 0

rules.name: Boolean structure size
rules.source_quote: Booleans may be packed into 32-bit structures
rules.test_hint: Send frames with boolean structures that are not 32 bits

rules.name: String length field size
rules.source_quote: The first 2 bytes of the string structure is a 16-bit unsigned integer, this value is the length of the string
rules.test_hint: Send frames with string length fields that are not 16 bits

rules.name: ASCII character encoding

constraint.value: ASCII characters, one character per byte

rules.source_quote: Strings are defined as a sequence of n ASCII characters. There is one ASCII character per byte
rules.test_hint: Send frames with non-ASCII characters or multi-byte character encodings in string fields

rules.name: String padding with zeros

constraint.value: The pad field places binary zeros in any remaining bytes to fill out the fixed size of the data structure

rules.source_quote: the pad field places binary zeros in any remaining bytes to fill out the fixed size of the data structure
rules.test_hint: Send frames with non-zero padding bytes in string structures

rules.name: Opaque data unused bytes must be zero

constraint.value: All unused bytes of an opaque data structure should be filled with binary zeros

rules.source_quote: All unused bytes of an opaque data structure should be filled with binary zeros.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with non-zero values in unused bytes of opaque data structures

rules.name: Variable opaque data length field size
rules.source_quote: The variable length opaque data structure is defined as a half word (16 bits) length field
rules.test_hint: Send frames with variable opaque data length fields that are not 16 bits

rules.name: Variable opaque data padding with zeros

constraint.value: The pad field places binary zeros in any remaining bytes to fill out the fixed size of the data structure

rules.source_quote: the pad field places binary zeros in any remaining bytes to fill out the fixed size of the data structure
rules.test_hint: Send frames with non-zero padding bytes in variable opaque data structures

rules.name: Valid transport layer port number range
rules.source_quote: Transport layer port assignments are therefore not critical and can be assigned by a system integrator using any values in the range 1 to 65535.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with transport port numbers outside the valid range (0 or greater than 65535)

rules.name: IANA assigned port number range
rules.source_quote: Assigned port numbers: 0 – 1023

rules.name: IANA registered port number range
rules.source_quote: Registered port numbers: 1024 – 49151

rules.name: Dynamic/Private port number range
rules.source_quote: Dynamic/Private port numbers: 49152 – 65535

rules.name: Reserved word alignment requirement
rules.source_quote: The Reserved word at the beginning of the message should be aligned on a 32-bit boundary.
rules.test_hint: Send messages where the Reserved word is not aligned on a 32-bit boundary

rules.name: Functional Status Sets alignment requirement
rules.source_quote: Functional Status Sets should also be aligned on 32-bit boundaries throughout the message.
rules.test_hint: Send messages where Functional Status Sets are not aligned on 32-bit boundaries

rules.name: Data element alignment by size

constraint.value: address_divisible_by_element_length

rules.source_quote: A data element is said to be aligned if the address of the element in memory is evenly divisible by the data element length (in bytes).
rules.test_hint: Send messages with data elements not aligned according to their size (e.g., 4-byte value not on address divisible by 4)

rules.name: Double precision float address alignment

constraint.value: address must be divisible by 8 bytes

rules.source_quote: next field (Double precision float – 64 bits) is at an address that is divisible by its length (8 bytes)
rules.test_hint: Generate frames with double precision float fields at addresses not divisible by 8 bytes

rules.name: Functional Status Set field size
rules.source_quote: The Functional Status Set (FSS) is a 32-bit field made up of four 8 bit status fields
rules.test_hint: Send frames with FSS fields that are not exactly 32 bits in size

rules.name: Status field size within FSS
rules.source_quote: The Functional Status Set (FSS) is a 32-bit field made up of four 8 bit status fields
rules.test_hint: Send frames with status fields within FSS that are not 8 bits each

rules.name: Unused status fields must be zero
rules.source_quote: If no other DS are used in a FDS, the remaining 24 bits of the FSS must be zeros
rules.test_hint: Send frames where unused status fields in FSS contain non-zero values

rules.name: Maximum data sets per FSS
rules.source_quote: each of the remaining status fields are used to represent health and status for them, up to 4 DS
rules.test_hint: Send frames with more than 4 data sets associated with a single FSS

rules.name: Functional status enumeration values
rules.source_quote: The FS is a byte of enumerated type with enumerations as defined in Table 1-2. Refer to Table 1-3 for the enumeration binary and decimal representations
rules.test_hint: Send frames with functional status values not in the allowed enumeration set

rules.name: Invalid data primitive invalidates entire data set

constraint.value: if one data primitive is invalid, entire data set must be marked invalid

rules.source_quote: if one data primitive is invalid, the entire Data Set has to be marked as invalid
rules.test_hint: Send frames where some data primitives are invalid but the data set status does not reflect this invalidity

rules.name: Status priority enforcement

constraint.value: when multiple conditions exist, highest priority condition must be encoded

rules.source_quote: When computing the functional status for a DS it is possible for more than one condition to exist. In that case the condition with the highest priority should be encoded into the status field. Priority 1 is the highest priority, priority 4 is the lowest
rules.test_hint: Send frames where multiple status conditions exist but lower priority status is encoded instead of higher priority

rules.name: data_primitive_packing

constraint.value: data primitives must be placed consecutively with no unused bytes between them except for alignment padding

rules.source_quote: Data primitives are placed in the data set one after another with no unused bytes between them except for padding for alignment purposes.
rules.test_hint: Create a message with unnecessary gaps between data primitives that are not for alignment purposes. Receivers may reject malformed data.

rules.name: spare_field_initialization

constraint.value: must be filled with binary zeros if unused

rules.source_quote: Spare data fields should be filled in with binary zeros if unused.
rules.test_hint: Send a message with spare fields containing non-zero data. Some receivers may validate spare field contents and reject invalid messages.

rules.name: reserved_field_initialization

constraint.value: 32-bit reserved field must be filled with all binary zeros

rules.source_quote: The 32-bit reserved field should be filled with all binary zeros.
rules.test_hint: Send a message with the 32-bit reserved field containing non-zero values. Receivers may validate this field and reject invalid messages.

rules.name: global_spare_initialization

constraint.value: must be filled with all binary zeros if included

rules.source_quote: If this field is included in a message, it should be filled with all binary zeros.
rules.test_hint: Send a message with a global spare field containing non-zero data. Some receivers may validate spare field contents and reject the message.

rules.name: Minimum Ethernet Payload Padding
rules.source_quote: The minimum size packet in Ethernet has a payload of 18 bytes. If a message is sent on an AFDX network that is less than 18 bytes long the message will be padded out to 18 bytes before it appears on the medium.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with payload less than 18 bytes and verify they are automatically padded to 18 bytes before transmission on the medium

rules.name: Parameter Removal Replacement Rule

constraint.value: replace_with_pad_no_shift

rules.source_quote: When removing a parameter from a data set, replace it with a pad. Do not shift the remainder of the message up and remove the place the parameter was filling.
rules.test_hint: Send messages where parameters have been removed by shifting remaining data instead of padding, and verify proper handling

rules.name: Parameter Addition Position Rule

constraint.value: insert_in_spare_or_pad_fields

rules.source_quote: Minimize the impact to the message by avoiding a shift of position of the existing message parameters, insert new parameters in spare or pad fields.
rules.test_hint: Send messages where new parameters cause shifts in existing parameter positions instead of using spare/pad fields

rules.name: Data Primitive Byte Order Rule

constraint.value: most_significant_byte_left

rules.source_quote: The boxes that represent a data primitive are intended to represent a group of bytes, the most significant byte on the left, the least significant byte on the right.
rules.test_hint: Send data primitives with incorrect byte ordering (least significant byte first) and verify rejection or correction

rules.name: Data Primitive Bit Order Rule

constraint.value: most_significant_bit_left

rules.source_quote: Also, the bits in the bytes are most significant bit on the left and least significant bit on the right.
rules.test_hint: Send data with incorrect bit ordering within bytes and verify proper handling or rejection

rules.name: Boolean data primitive bit ordering

constraint.value: packed_booleans_right_justified_fill_right_to_left

rules.source_quote: Packed Booleans are right justified, they begin filling in bits from right to left with spare on the left.
rules.test_hint: Generate frames with Boolean data primitives that have incorrect bit ordering (left-justified instead of right-justified)

rules.name: Optional features not applicable in AFDX
rules.source_quote: For AFDX, the column "OPTIONAL" is not used. It is replaced by "NOT APPLICABLE" in order to identify the requirements that do not apply to an AFDX End System, e.g., IP options and router requirements. NOT APPLICABLE should be interpreted as MUST NOT.
rules.source_section: Attachment 2 - IP/ICMP, UDP, AND TCP PROFILE PROVISIONS
rules.test_hint: Send frames using TCP features marked as NOT APPLICABLE/MUST NOT in AFDX networks

rules.name: TCP may aggregate unpushed data

constraint.value: may_aggregate_data_without_push_flag

rules.source_quote: When an application issues a series of SEND calls without setting the PUSH flag, the TCP MAY aggregate the data internally without sending it. Similarly, when a series of Segments is received without the PSH bit, a TCP MAY queue the data internally without passing it to the receiving application.
rules.test_hint: Send TCP segments without PUSH flag and verify aggregation behavior matches AFDX requirements

rules.name: TCP must set PUSH bit in last buffered segment
rules.source_quote: MUST set the PSH bit in the last buffered segment (i.e., when there is no more queued data to be sent).
rules.test_hint: Send TCP data without setting PUSH bit in the final segment when no more data is queued

rules.name: TCP should send maximum size segments when possible

constraint.value: should_send_maximum_sized_segment

rules.source_quote: However, a TCP SHOULD send a maximum-sized segment whenever possible, to improve performance
rules.test_hint: Send TCP segments that are intentionally smaller than maximum possible size when larger segments could be sent

rules.name: Window size unsigned treatment

constraint.value: must be treated as unsigned number

rules.source_quote: The window size MUST be treated as an unsigned number.
rules.test_hint: Send TCP segments with window size values that would be negative if interpreted as signed but positive as unsigned

rules.name: No window shrinking from right

constraint.value: receiver should not move right window edge to the left

rules.source_quote: A TCP receiver SHOULD NOT shrink the window, i.e., move the right window edge to the left.
rules.test_hint: Generate sequence where receiver shrinks window by moving right edge leftward and observe if network handles this violation

rules.name: Sender robust against window shrinking

constraint.value: must be robust against window shrinking that makes useable window negative

rules.source_quote: However, a sending TCP MUST be robust against window shrinking, which may cause "useable window" (see Section 4.2.3.4) to become negative
rules.test_hint: Force window shrinking that creates negative useable window and verify sender handles it gracefully

rules.name: Zero window probing support required
rules.source_quote: Probing of zero (offered) windows MUST be supported.
rules.test_hint: Create zero window condition and verify that sender generates window probe packets

rules.name: First zero window probe timing

constraint.value: first probe should be sent after retransmission timeout period

rules.source_quote: The transmitting host SHOULD send the first zero-window probe when a zero window has existed for the retransmission timeout period.
rules.test_hint: Set zero window and measure timing of first probe relative to RTO to verify compliance

rules.name: Exponential backoff for zero window probes

constraint.value: exponentially increase interval between successive probes

rules.source_quote: The transmitting host SHOULD increase exponentially the interval between successive probes.
rules.test_hint: Monitor multiple zero window probe intervals to verify exponential backoff pattern

rules.name: Urgent pointer points to last octet

constraint.value: points to sequence number of last octet, not last+1

rules.source_quote: The urgent pointer points to the sequence number of the LAST octet (not LAST+1)
rules.test_hint: Send urgent data with pointer incorrectly pointing to LAST+1 instead of LAST octet

rules.name: Support arbitrary length urgent data

constraint.value: must support urgent data sequence of any length

rules.source_quote: A TCP MUST support a sequence of urgent data of any length.
rules.test_hint: Send extremely long urgent data sequences to test length handling limits

rules.name: Receive TCP option in any segment
rules.source_quote: A TCP MUST be able to receive a TCP option in any segment.
rules.test_hint: Send TCP options in unexpected segment types to verify proper handling

rules.name: Ignore unsupported options

constraint.value: must ignore without error any unimplemented option with length field

rules.source_quote: A TCP MUST ignore without error any TCP option it does not implement, assuming that the option has a length field.
rules.test_hint: Send segments with unrecognized TCP options to verify they are silently ignored

rules.name: Default MSS value
rules.source_quote: If an MSS option is not received at connection setup, TCP MUST assume a default send MSS of 536.
rules.test_hint: Establish connections without MSS option and verify 536-byte MSS is assumed

rules.name: Sender must generate checksum
rules.source_quote: The sender MUST generate.
rules.test_hint: Send TCP segments with missing or zero checksums to test sender compliance

rules.name: Receiver must check checksum
rules.source_quote: The receiver MUST check it.
rules.test_hint: Send TCP segments with incorrect checksums to verify receiver rejects them

rules.name: Use clock-driven ISN selection

constraint.value: must use specified clock-driven selection

rules.source_quote: A TCP MUST use the specified clock-driven selection of initial sequence numbers.
rules.test_hint: Analyze ISN patterns across connections to verify proper clock-driven randomization

rules.name: simultaneous_open_support

constraint.value: TCP must support simultaneous open attempts

rules.source_quote: A TCP MUST support simultaneous open attempts.
rules.test_hint: Send simultaneous SYN packets from both ends and verify the connection establishes correctly

rules.name: syn_rcvd_state_tracking

constraint.value: TCP implementation must keep track of whether a connection has reached SYN_RCVD state as the result of a passive OPEN or an active OPEN

rules.source_quote: TCP implementation MUST keep track of whether a connection has reached SYN_RCVD state as the result of a passive OPEN or an active OPEN.
rules.test_hint: Test different sequences of active/passive opens and verify state tracking is maintained correctly

rules.name: passive_open_isolation

constraint.value: Every passive OPEN call must not affect any previously created connection record

rules.source_quote: Every passive OPEN call it MUST NOT affect any previously created connection record.
rules.test_hint: Create multiple passive opens on same port and verify existing connections remain unaffected

rules.name: reject_broadcast_multicast_open

constraint.value: TCP implementation must reject as an error a local OPEN call for an invalid remote IP address (e.g., a broadcast or multicast address)

rules.source_quote: A TCP implementation MUST reject as an error a local OPEN call for an invalid remote IP address (e.g., a broadcast or multicast address).
rules.test_hint: Attempt to open TCP connection to broadcast or multicast address and verify it is rejected

rules.name: discard_syn_to_broadcast_multicast

constraint.value: TCP implementation must silently discard an incoming SYN segment that is addressed to a broadcast or multicast address

rules.source_quote: A TCP implementation MUST silently discard an incoming SYN segment that is addressed to a broadcast or multicast address.
rules.test_hint: Send SYN segment to broadcast/multicast address and verify it is silently discarded

rules.name: inform_application_of_aborted_connection

constraint.value: If a TCP connection is closed by the remote site, the local application must be informed whether it closed normally or was aborted

rules.source_quote: If a TCP connection is closed by the remote site, the local application MUST be informed whether it closed normally or was aborted.
rules.test_hint: Close connection remotely with RST vs FIN and verify application receives correct close indication

rules.name: time_wait_duration

constraint.value: 2 * MSL

rules.source_quote: When a connection is closed actively, it MUST linger in TIME-WAIT state for a time 2xMSL.
rules.test_hint: Close connection actively and verify it remains in TIME-WAIT for exactly 2*MSL seconds

rules.name: Initial Round Trip Time
rules.source_quote: RTT = 0 seconds.
rules.test_hint: Configure TCP connection with non-zero initial RTT value

rules.name: Initial Retransmission Timeout
rules.source_quote: RTO = 3 seconds.
rules.test_hint: Configure TCP connection with different initial RTO value

rules.name: Maximum Retransmission Timeout Upper Bound
rules.source_quote: the upper bound should be 2*MSL, i.e., 240 seconds.
rules.test_hint: Configure TCP with RTO upper bound exceeding 240 seconds

rules.name: Maximum ACK Delay
rules.source_quote: The delay MUST be less than 0.5 seconds.
rules.test_hint: Configure delayed ACK with delay exceeding 0.5 seconds

rules.name: Minimum ACK Frequency for Full Segments
rules.source_quote: In a stream of full-sized segments there SHOULD be an ACK for at least every second segment.
rules.test_hint: Send stream of full-size segments with ACK frequency less than every second segment

rules.name: Default Time to Live
rules.source_quote: Not used in AFDX, default value is 1
rules.test_hint: Send TCP segments with TTL value other than 1

rules.name: Minimum R1 Retransmission Threshold
rules.source_quote: The value of R1 SHOULD correspond to at least 3 retransmissions, at the current RTO.
rules.test_hint: Configure R1 threshold below 3 retransmissions

rules.name: Minimum R2 Connection Close Threshold
rules.source_quote: The value of R2 SHOULD correspond to at least 100 seconds.
rules.test_hint: Configure R2 threshold below 100 seconds

rules.name: Minimum SYN R2 Threshold
rules.source_quote: R2 for a SYN segment MUST be set large enough to provide retransmission of the segment for at least 3 minutes.
rules.test_hint: Configure SYN R2 threshold below 180 seconds (3 minutes)

rules.name: ACK Aggregation Required

constraint.value: must_aggregate_acks

rules.source_quote: In general, the processing of received segments MUST be implemented to aggregate ACK segments whenever possible.
rules.test_hint: Send multiple segments that could be aggregated and verify ACK behavior

rules.name: Receiver SWS Avoidance Required
rules.source_quote: A TCP MUST include a SWS avoidance algorithm in the receiver.
rules.test_hint: Test receiver behavior with small window updates to verify SWS avoidance

rules.name: ICMP message type restriction
rules.source_quote: Only ICMP "echo request" and "echo reply" are allowed.
rules.source_section: Attachment 2 - IP/ICMP, UDP, AND TCP Profile Provisions
rules.test_hint: Send ICMP messages other than echo request/reply (e.g., destination unreachable, time exceeded, parameter problem) and verify they are rejected

rules.name: Invalid remote IP address rejection

constraint.value: must_reject_invalid_remote_ip

rules.source_quote: A TCP implementation MUST reject as an error a local OPEN call for an invalid remote IP address.
rules.test_hint: Attempt TCP connection to invalid IP addresses and verify the connection is rejected

rules.name: Invalid source address SYN rejection

constraint.value: must_ignore_syn_with_invalid_source

rules.source_quote: An incoming SYN with an invalid source address must be ignored either by TCP or by the IP layer.
rules.test_hint: Send TCP SYN packets with invalid source IP addresses and verify they are ignored

rules.name: Broadcast/multicast SYN silently discarded

constraint.value: must_silently_discard_broadcast_multicast_syn

rules.source_quote: A TCP implementation MUST silently discard an incoming SYN segment that is addressed to a broadcast or multicast address.
rules.test_hint: Send TCP SYN packets to broadcast or multicast addresses and verify they are silently discarded without any response

rules.name: UDP port unreachable message prohibition
rules.source_quote: If a datagram arrives addressed to a UDP port for which there is no pending LISTEN call, UDP SHOULD send an ICMP Port Unreachable message. [AFDX: NOT APPLICABLE - Only ICMP "echo request" and "echo reply" are allowed.]
rules.source_section: Table 2-2 - Transport Layer UDP Requirements Summary
rules.test_hint: Send UDP datagrams to non-listening ports and verify that ICMP Port Unreachable messages are not generated

rules.name: IP options prohibition
rules.source_quote: IP options are not used in AFDX
rules.source_section: Table 2-2 - Transport Layer UDP Requirements Summary
rules.test_hint: Send IP datagrams with various IP options (source routing, timestamp, etc.) and verify they are either stripped or cause frame rejection

rules.name: TOS field prohibition
rules.source_quote: TOS is not used by AFDX
rules.test_hint: Send TCP segments with non-zero TOS values and verify they are ignored or cause rejection

rules.name: UDP checksum prohibition
rules.source_quote: Checksum is not used in AFDX
rules.source_section: Table 2-2 - Transport Layer UDP Requirements Summary
rules.test_hint: Send UDP datagrams with various checksum values (valid, invalid, zero) and verify that checksum validation is not performed

rules.name: ICMP echo request processing requirement

constraint.value: must_pass_to_application_layer

rules.source_quote: UDP MUST pass to the application layer all ICMP error messages that it receives from the IP layer. [AFDX: Only for ICMP "echo request".]
rules.source_section: Table 2-2 - Transport Layer UDP Requirements Summary
rules.test_hint: Send ICMP echo requests and verify they are processed and passed to the application layer, while other ICMP messages are not

rules.name: Invalid IP source address rejection

constraint.value: reject_broadcast_multicast_addresses

rules.source_quote: A UDP datagram received with an invalid IP source address (e.g., a broadcast or multicast address) must be discarded by UDP or by the IP layer.
rules.source_section: Table 2-2 - Transport Layer UDP Requirements Summary
rules.test_hint: Send UDP datagrams with broadcast or multicast source addresses and verify they are silently discarded

rules.name: Valid IP source address requirement for transmission

constraint.value: must_be_host_address

rules.source_quote: When a host sends a UDP datagram, the source address MUST be (one of) the IP address(es) of the host.
rules.source_section: Table 2-2 - Transport Layer UDP Requirements Summary
rules.test_hint: Verify that outgoing UDP datagrams use only valid host IP addresses as source addresses, not foreign or invalid addresses

rules.name: IP Version Field Validation
rules.source_quote: A datagram whose version number is not 4 MUST be silently discarded.
rules.test_hint: Send IP datagrams with version field set to values other than 4 (e.g., 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 15)

rules.name: IP Header Checksum Verification

constraint.value: must_verify_and_discard_on_error

rules.source_quote: A host MUST verify the IP header checksum on every received datagram and silently discard every datagram that has a bad checksum.
rules.test_hint: Send IP datagrams with intentionally corrupted header checksums

rules.name: Source Address Must Be Own IP Address

constraint.value: must_be_own_ip_not_broadcast_multicast

rules.source_quote: When a host sends any datagram, the IP source address MUST be one of its own IP addresses (but not a broadcast or multicast address).
rules.test_hint: Send frames with source IP addresses that are not assigned to the sending interface, or use broadcast/multicast addresses as source

rules.name: Discard Datagram With Bad Destination Address

constraint.value: silently_discard_if_not_destined_for_host

rules.source_quote: A host MUST silently discard an incoming datagram that is not destined for the host.
rules.test_hint: Send frames to IP addresses that are not assigned to any interface on the receiving end system

rules.name: Must Not Send Packet With TTL Zero
rules.source_quote: A host MUST NOT send a datagram with a Time-to-Live (TTL) value of zero.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to send frames with TTL field set to 0

rules.name: TTL Minimum Acceptance Rule
rules.source_quote: A host MUST NOT discard a datagram just because it was received with TTL less than 2.
rules.test_hint: Send IP datagrams with TTL=1 to verify they are not discarded based solely on low TTL value

rules.name: Unknown IP Options Handling

constraint.value: silently_ignore_unknown_options

rules.source_quote: The IP and transport layer MUST each interpret those IP options that they understand and silently ignore the others.
rules.test_hint: Send IP datagrams with unrecognized option types to verify they are silently ignored without generating errors

rules.name: Stream Identifier Option Handling

constraint.value: silently_ignore_if_received

rules.source_quote: ...and it MUST be silently ignored if received.
rules.test_hint: Send IP datagrams containing Stream Identifier option to verify it is silently ignored

rules.name: Multiple Source Route Options Prohibition
rules.source_quote: An IP header containing more than one Source Route option MUST NOT be sent.
rules.test_hint: Send IP datagrams with multiple Source Route options to test rejection or handling

rules.name: Unknown ICMP Type Handling

constraint.value: silently_discard_unknown_types

rules.source_quote: If an ICMP message of unknown type is received, it MUST be silently discarded.
rules.test_hint: Send ICMP messages with undefined or reserved type values to verify they are silently discarded

rules.name: ICMP Error Payload Minimum
rules.source_quote: Every ICMP error message includes the Internet header and at least the first 8 data octets of the datagram that triggered the error; more than 8 octets MAY be sent.
rules.test_hint: Generate conditions that trigger ICMP errors and verify the error message contains at least 8 octets of original datagram data

rules.name: ICMP Message Type Limitation
rules.source_quote: Only ICMP "echo request" and "echo reply" are allowed.
rules.source_section: Attachment 2 - IP/ICMP, UDP, and TCP Profile Provisions
rules.test_hint: Send ICMP messages other than echo request/reply (e.g., destination unreachable, source quench, time exceeded, parameter problem) to verify they are rejected

rules.name: ICMP Error Message Prohibition
rules.source_quote: No ICMP errors
rules.source_section: Attachment 2 - IP/ICMP, UDP, and TCP Profile Provisions
rules.test_hint: Attempt to trigger ICMP error generation (invalid IP headers, unreachable destinations, etc.) and verify no ICMP error messages are sent

rules.name: ICMP Redirect Prohibition from End Systems
rules.source_quote: No ICMP redirect from ES
rules.source_section: Attachment 2 - IP/ICMP, UDP, and TCP Profile Provisions
rules.test_hint: Configure an End System to attempt sending ICMP redirect messages and verify they are not transmitted

rules.name: Invalid Source Address Rejection

constraint.value: must_not_accept_invalid_source_addresses

rules.source_quote: a datagram whose source address does not define a single host -- e.g., a zero address, a loopback address, a broadcast address, a multicast address, or a Class address.
rules.source_section: Attachment 2 - IP/ICMP, UDP, and TCP Profile Provisions
rules.test_hint: Send frames with invalid source addresses (0.0.0.0, loopback, broadcast, multicast addresses) and verify they are rejected

rules.name: ICMP Message Type Limitation
rules.source_quote: Only ICMP "echo request" and "echo reply" are allowed.
rules.test_hint: Send ICMP messages other than echo request/reply (e.g., destination unreachable, time exceeded) and verify they are rejected or dropped

rules.name: Echo Reply Source Address Requirement

constraint.value: source_address_must_match_request_destination

rules.source_quote: The IP source address in an ICMP Echo Reply MUST be the same as the specific-destination address (defined in Section 3.2.1.3) of the corresponding ICMP Echo Request message.
rules.test_hint: Send echo request to one IP address and generate echo reply with different source IP address to verify proper validation

rules.name: Echo Reply Data Completeness

constraint.value: reply_must_include_complete_request_data

rules.source_quote: Data received in an ICMP Echo Request MUST be entirely included in the resulting Echo Reply.
rules.test_hint: Send echo request with specific data payload and verify echo reply contains exactly the same data without truncation or modification

rules.name: Broadcast Echo Request Discard

constraint.value: may_silently_discard_broadcast_requests

rules.source_quote: An ICMP Echo Request destined to an IP broadcast or IP multicast address MAY be silently discarded.
rules.test_hint: Send echo requests to broadcast/multicast addresses and verify they may be discarded without response or error message

rules.name: Source Route Option Processing in Echo Reply

constraint.value: must_reverse_source_route_for_reply

rules.source_quote: If a Source Route option is received in an ICMP Echo Request, the return route MUST be reversed and used as a Source Route option for the Echo Reply message.
rules.test_hint: Send echo request with source route option and verify the echo reply reverses the route correctly

rules.name: ICMP Message Type Restriction
rules.source_quote: Only ICMP "echo request" and "echo reply" are allowed.
rules.test_hint: Send ICMP messages other than echo request/reply (e.g., timestamp request, address mask request) and verify they are rejected or dropped

rules.name: ICMP Timestamp Request Prohibition
rules.source_quote: Only ICMP "echo request" and "echo reply" are allowed.
rules.test_hint: Send ICMP timestamp request messages and verify they are rejected or not processed

rules.name: ICMP Timestamp Reply Prohibition
rules.source_quote: Only ICMP "echo request" and "echo reply" are allowed.
rules.test_hint: Send ICMP timestamp reply messages and verify they are rejected or not processed

rules.name: ICMP Address Mask Request Prohibition
rules.source_quote: Only ICMP "echo request" and "echo reply" are allowed.
rules.test_hint: Send ICMP address mask request messages and verify they are rejected or not processed

rules.name: ICMP Address Mask Reply Prohibition
rules.source_quote: Only ICMP "echo request" and "echo reply" are allowed.
rules.test_hint: Send ICMP address mask reply messages and verify they are rejected or not processed

rules.name: Unauthorized Address Mask Reply Prohibition

constraint.value: A system MUST NOT send an Address Mask Reply unless it is an authoritative agent for address masks

rules.source_quote: A system MUST NOT send an Address Mask Reply unless it is an authoritative agent for address masks.
rules.test_hint: Configure a non-authoritative system to send address mask replies and verify this is prevented or rejected

rules.name: No gateway operation requirement
rules.source_quote: The host IP layer MUST operate correctly in a minimal network environment, and in particular, when there are no gateways.
rules.test_hint: Configure network without gateways and verify proper operation; attempt to introduce gateway functionality and verify it is not used

rules.name: Static routing requirement
rules.source_quote: AFDX is statically defined
rules.test_hint: Attempt to send dynamic routing protocol messages or ICMP redirects to verify they are ignored and routing remains static

rules.name: Route cache maintenance prohibition

constraint.value: no_dynamic_updates_allowed

rules.source_quote: To efficiently route a series of datagrams to the same destination, the source host MUST keep a "route cache" of mappings to next-hop gateways.
rules.test_hint: Send packets that would normally trigger route cache updates in standard IP networks and verify the cache remains unchanged

rules.name: Gateway failure detection not required
rules.source_quote: The IP layer MUST be able to detect the failure of a "next-hop" gateway that is listed in its route cache and to choose an alternate gateway.
rules.test_hint: Simulate gateway failures and verify that AFDX systems do not implement dynamic failure detection or recovery mechanisms

rules.name: Continuous gateway pinging prohibition
rules.source_quote: In particular, hosts MUST NOT actively check the status of a first-hop gateway by simply pinging the gateway continuously.
rules.test_hint: Monitor network traffic for continuous ICMP echo requests to gateways and verify such behavior is not implemented

rules.name: minimum reassembly buffer size
rules.source_quote: EMTU_R MUST be greater than or equal to 576
rules.test_hint: Send IP datagrams larger than the configured EMTU_R to test reassembly buffer overflow

rules.name: discard partially-reassembled datagram on timeout

constraint.value: discard_partial_datagram_on_timeout

rules.source_quote: If this timeout expires, the partially-reassembled datagram MUST be discarded
rules.test_hint: Send fragmented IP datagrams with missing fragments to test timeout behavior and partial datagram cleanup

rules.name: maximum datagram size without fragmentation

constraint.value: do_not_exceed_MMS_S

rules.source_quote: A host that does not implement local fragmentation MUST ensure that the transport layer (for TCP) or the application layer (for UDP) obtains MMS_S from the IP layer and does not send a datagram exceeding MMS_S in size
rules.test_hint: Send UDP datagrams larger than MMS_S to test size enforcement when local fragmentation is not implemented

rules.name: maximum datagram size to off-network destinations
rules.source_quote: In the absence of actual knowledge of the minimum MTU along the path, the IP layer SHOULD use EMTU_S <= 576 whenever the destination address is not on a connected network
rules.test_hint: Send datagrams larger than 576 bytes to off-network destinations to test MTU enforcement

rules.name: silently discard datagrams on wrong interface

constraint.value: discard_if_destination_address_mismatch_interface

rules.source_quote: A host MAY silently discard an incoming datagram whose destination address does not correspond to the physical interface through which it is received
rules.test_hint: Send IP datagrams with destination addresses that don't match the receiving interface to test interface validation

rules.name: restrict outgoing datagrams to correct interface

constraint.value: send_only_through_matching_interface

rules.source_quote: A host MAY restrict itself to sending (non-source-routed) IP datagrams only through the physical interface that corresponds to the IP source address of the datagrams
rules.test_hint: Attempt to send IP datagrams with source addresses that don't match the outgoing interface to test source address validation

rules.name: source routing not allowed
rules.source_quote: Source routing not allowed
rules.test_hint: Send IP datagrams with Source Route Options to test that they are rejected or filtered

rules.name: IP options not used
rules.source_quote: Options are not used.
rules.source_section: Attachment 2 - IP/ICMP, UDP, and TCP Profile Provisions
rules.test_hint: Send IP datagrams with options fields (Record Route, Timestamp, etc.) to verify they are rejected or ignored

rules.name: Broadcast address not allowed as source

constraint.value: broadcast addresses must not be used as source address

rules.source_quote: Broadcast address as IP source address
rules.source_section: Attachment 2 - IP/ICMP, UDP, and TCP Profile Provisions
rules.test_hint: Send IP datagrams with broadcast addresses (limited broadcast, directed broadcast, etc.) as the source address to verify they are rejected

rules.name: Standard broadcast address formats
rules.source_quote: Section 3.2.1.3 defined the four standard IP broadcast address forms: * Limited Broadcast: {-1, -1} * Directed Broadcast: {<Network-number>,-1} * Subnet Directed Broadcast: {<Network-number>,<Subnet-number>,-1} * All-Subnets Directed Broadcast: {<Network-number>,-1,-1}
rules.source_section: Attachment 2 - IP/ICMP, UDP, and TCP Profile Provisions
rules.test_hint: Send datagrams with non-standard broadcast address formats to verify proper recognition and handling

rules.name: Domain ID value restrictions
rules.source_quote: The Domain ID should be coded with 4 bits. The 0000 and 1111 are forbidden values. Therefore, 14 Domains ID are possible.
rules.test_hint: Generate frames with Domain ID set to forbidden values 0 (0000) or 15 (1111)

rules.name: Side ID value restrictions
rules.source_quote: The Side ID format should be coded with 3 bits. The 000 and 111 are forbidden values.
rules.test_hint: Generate frames with Side ID set to forbidden values 0 (000) or 7 (111)

rules.name: Location ID value restrictions
rules.source_quote: The Location ID format should be coded with 5 bits. The 00000 and 11111 are forbidden values.
rules.test_hint: Generate frames with Location ID set to forbidden values 0 (00000) or 31 (11111)

rules.name: MAC address constant field format
rules.test_hint: Generate frames with MAC addresses that do not start with the required constant field 0x020000

rules.name: IP address class and private network format
rules.source_quote: Class A 1-bit Private IP address 7-bits "0" "0001010"
rules.test_hint: Generate frames with IP addresses that do not conform to the 10.x.x.x private Class A format

rules.name: ARINC 429 data conversion preference

constraint.value: ARINC 429 data should be converted to permitted AFDX data elements at gateway

rules.source_quote: The preferred way to put ARINC 429 data on an AFDX network is to convert the individual parameters into one of the permitted AFDX data elements of Table 1-1.0. Every effort should be made to do this at the gateway where ARINC 429 and AFDX meet.
rules.test_hint: Send ARINC 429 data that is not converted to permitted AFDX data elements and verify gateway behavior

rules.name: Single label message structure

constraint.value: 32-bit opaque data primitive for single ARINC 429 label

rules.source_quote: Place each label in a fixed length 32-bit opaque data primitive
rules.test_hint: Send single ARINC 429 labels in formats other than 32-bit opaque data primitive

rules.name: Variable length multiple label structure

constraint.value: variable length opaque structure for multiple ARINC 429 labels

rules.source_quote: Place a varying number of labels in a variable length opaque structure
rules.test_hint: Send multiple ARINC 429 labels in fixed length structures instead of variable length

rules.name: Gateway status indication

constraint.value: FS field represents status of gateway introducing ARINC 429 data to AFDX network

rules.source_quote: Note that the FS represents the status of the gateway that is introducing the ARINC 429 data to the AFDX network.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with incorrect or missing FS status information for gateway status

rules.name: ARINC 429 device status indication

constraint.value: ARINC 429 device status presented in the label itself

rules.source_quote: The status of the ARINC 429 device is presented in the label.
rules.test_hint: Send ARINC 429 labels with corrupted or missing device status information

rules.name: Individual device status via SSM

constraint.value: Status of devices generating ARINC 429 labels indicated in individual labels by SSM field

rules.source_quote: the status of the devices that generated the ARINC 429 labels is indicated in the individual labels by means of the SSM field
rules.test_hint: Send ARINC 429 labels with incorrect or missing SSM status fields

rules.name: Single DS for single threaded device

constraint.value: Single DS should be used if all labels concentrated by single threaded device

rules.source_quote: If all labels are concentrated into a single Ethernet frame by a single threaded device, a single DS should be used
rules.test_hint: Send frames using multiple DS when all labels come from single threaded device

rules.name: Multiple DS for partial failure scenarios

constraint.value: Multiple DS should be used when concentrator portion could fail causing some labels to be invalid while frame remains legal

rules.source_quote: If the concentrator device is designed in such a way that a portion of it could fail in some way that causes some labels to be invalid, but a completely legal Ethernet frame is still generated with some valid labels, more than one DS should be considered.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with single DS when concentrator design allows partial failures affecting some labels

rules.name: Label ordering in gateway transmission

constraint.value: Labels presented in order received by gateway for transparent operation

rules.source_quote: The labels are presented in the order received by the gateway so the gateway and AFDX network are essentially transparent.
rules.test_hint: Send labels in different order than received at gateway and verify consumer processing

rules.name: Label placement in opaque structure

constraint.value: Labels placed one after another beginning with byte after length and pad fields

rules.source_quote: As labels arrive at the gateway, they are placed one after another in the opaque structure beginning with the byte after the length field and pad field.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with labels placed in incorrect positions within the opaque structure

rules.name: Length field computation

constraint.value: Gateway computes bytes of static length with good data and loads into length field

rules.source_quote: When it is time for transmission, the gateway will compute how many bytes of the static length have good data in them and load this number into the length field of the structure.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with incorrect length field values that don't match actual data content

rules.name: Unused portion padding

constraint.value: unused portion of opaque field filled with binary zeros

rules.source_quote: The unused portion of the opaque field is filled with binary zeros.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with non-zero values in unused portions of opaque fields

rules.name: Complete structure transmission

constraint.value: Entire static structure transmitted, not just used portion

rules.source_quote: The message is then sent, with the entire static structure, not just the used portion.
rules.test_hint: Send frames containing only the used portion of structure instead of entire static structure

rules.name: static message length for jitter reduction

constraint.value: messages should use statically defined structure length even if actual data is shorter to reduce jitter

rules.source_quote: Sending the complete, statically defined structure, helps keep the jitter in the system lower. This makes every message the same length, even though the data in the message is not all valid.
rules.test_hint: Send messages with variable lengths instead of using the full statically allocated size to increase jitter

rules.name: bandwidth allocated for maximum message size

constraint.value: bandwidth is allocated for maximum possible message size and cannot be used by other flows

rules.source_quote: The bandwidth has been allocated to this data flow for the maximum size the message can be, and is not useable by any other flow. It is therefore not wasted.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to use bandwidth allocated to one flow for another flow to test bandwidth isolation

rules.name: packet size limited by MTU

constraint.value: packet size must not exceed network MTU, oversized datagrams must be fragmented

rules.source_quote: Maximum size of a packet is limited by the MTU (Max Transfer Unit) of the network. Whenever an UDP datagram is too long to fit in a packet, it is break in an almost arbitrary number of pieces that are placed in fragments.
rules.test_hint: Send packets larger than the configured MTU to test fragmentation handling or rejection

rules.name: UDP datagram encapsulation in IP

constraint.value: UDP datagrams must be encapsulated inside IP datagrams for transmission

rules.source_quote: Application data are transmitted by encapsulation inside an UDP datagram or a TCP segment... To be transmitted end-to-end through the AFDX, a message must be encapsulated inside an IP datagram.
rules.test_hint: Send malformed encapsulation structures or skip required encapsulation layers

rules.name: frame composition at ethernet level

constraint.value: frame consists of MAC header followed by packet data

rules.source_quote: A frame is the unit of transmission at Ethernet level, and consists of a MAC header followed by a packet.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with missing MAC headers, corrupted MAC headers, or incorrect frame structure
